秦弱兰成名显德五年。

en:
Qin Ruolan became famous in 958 CE. 
During that year, Tao Gu, a government scholar, was ordered to go to Jinling. With the government behind him, he was arrogant wherever he went. Several months later, Li Jing held a feast for him in Clearheart Hall and asked Tao Gu to drink from a giant bell, but Tao Gu ignored him. Li Jing lamented that the kingdom was about to fall. 
Then he asked Ruolan to come out. She played music, sang, made tea, and poured wine for Tao Gu. Tao was ashamed and drank the wine. Everyone then wanted to see what Ruolan looked like, and thought while she was beautiful, her beauty was not celestial. However, by the end of the feast, they were all entranced by her, and since then have never forgotten about her. 
They finally realized that delicate flowers speak in the language of charm, and where beauty walks, hearts are never free.

回程路上，倒有一马猴骑猪而来，掷果于我们脚下！此猴莫非是猪之友？竟代猪报恩……比之人性，更有可敬者！
en:
We entered the mountains today in search of minerals. As we traversed a barren valley, we were startled by an odd sound. Looking toward it, we saw a wild boar hopelessly stuck in a crevice, unable to budge. We exerted monumental effort to yank it free, narrowly avoiding getting bitten by the beast. Though our search for ore proved fruitless, saving the boar's life was certainly an act of good karma.
On the journey back, a monkey came riding atop that same boar, throwing fresh fruit at our feet! Is this monkey perhaps a companion to the boar? To think it would repay our kindness on the boar's behalf... Such behavior is far more admirable than what we often see in human nature!

As Zhang Hu wrote, "Even without rain, the mountains remain damp. Even without clouds, the waters lie in shadow. Wild moss swallows the Broken Bridge, and fallen flowers pile high in the empty courtyard."
Because of Hangzhou's mild climate, snow is a rare sight. But when a heavy overnight snow does fall, the mist-shrouded willows along the banks turn stark white, and the frost-laden grass drapes the water like a silk sash. The silver bridge, blanketed in untouched snow, creates an absolutely breathtaking winter scene.

A Word from Your Editor
(with a humble bow)

Hey there, friend!

鹤助城防，多有败绩。非机关术不精妙，而是所赴之地皆多危急。后多收弟子，授城防术以为助力。然而大势难违，弟子之中，有驰援各处者，有见事不成弃而去者，又有折损战死者。
来来去去，锥心蚀骨。
一日鹤又吃败绩，流矢袭来，恰中腰间昔日鸦所赠司南佩，佩碎而人存。仓皇之间，不及捡拾，仍忙于迁移百姓之事。待至安全之地，方觉怅然。
不想百姓自寻一黑石，仿刻此佩，复赠于鹤。
鹤摩挲良久，此后随身，寸步未离。
“先生，为吾等弟子之司南。”
“百姓，为吾之司南。”
en:
Crane helped with city defense, but often failed. Not because his mechanisms weren't exquisite, but because the places he went were often in dire straits. Later, he took on many disciples, teaching them city defense techniques to help. However, the tide was difficult to turn. Among his disciples, some went to aid various places, some abandoned him and left when things failed, and others died in battle.
They came and went, piercing his heart.
One day, Crane suffered another defeat. A stray arrow came flying, hitting the compass pendant that Raven had given him, which he wore at his waist. The pendant broke, but Crane survived. In the chaos, he couldn't stop to pick it up, still busy evacuating the people. Only when he reached safety did he feel the loss.
Unexpectedly, the people found a black stone, carved a replica of the pendant, and gave it back to Crane.
Crane rubbed it for a long time. Afterwards, he kept it with him, never leaving it.
"Sir, you are the compass for us disciples."
"The people are my compass."

zh:
叶万山铁心将军的名号，最初是那些敬仰他的百姓给他的。
铁心二字，是军心如铁、刚正不移。纵使妻女被契丹掠走要挟，纵使家破人亡，他也不曾低头投降。
因为若是以他一家的牺牲，可以守住一城百姓安宁，那就值得。
可城还是没守住。
契丹的兵马太壮太肥，他拼尽全力，定州依然失陷。

叶万山退兵的那一日，他明白过来，单凭他一人之力，做不到守土安邦，更做不到收回失地。唯有等待朝廷的主力，一同北上。
于是他等了十三年，十三年里，噩梦缠身，唯一能够握紧的只有手中的刀，一遍又一遍，练习挥斩。
所幸，后来他终于等到了，周世宗北伐。

叶万山重新穿上日夜擦拭的铠甲，带着一手操练的天虎军，整装城下，以盼大军。
可谁知北伐竟然半途而废。

怎么可以……
怎么可以？
他妻子、女儿、儿子，都没了，熬了那么多年，边城的百姓受苦那么多年，怎么可以，说不北伐、便不北伐？
……必须要北伐，若是那些躲在后方的懦夫不敢北伐，那他叶万山，便逼他们北伐。

叶万山调转马头，将刀刃，转向城中百姓的方向。黑云蔽日、天光微弱，谁也看不清他脸上的表情。
若以一城百姓的牺牲，可以守住天下百姓的安宁……那，就值得。
那一夜，没有外敌来犯，但却有人见到契丹入城，痛苦的嚎哭声响彻了这个叶万山蛰居十三年的小城。
铁心将军的铁心，从此变成了铁石心肠的铁心。

后来，叶万山入清河佛寺静修，那个和尚与他说，渡过菩提苦海，便是幸福的彼岸。
可他看，这苦海，他是渡不过去了。
en:
Ye Wanshan, the man known as General Ironheart, earns his title from the people who admire his unyielding spirit.
"Ironheart" encapsulates his firm resolve and unshakable will that refuses to bend. Even when his beloved wife and daughter are captured by the Khitan and used as leverage against him, he does not waver. His family is torn apart, yet he never once thinks of surrendering.
Their sacrifice was justified if it meant ensuring the peace of his city and safeguarding its people.
But even with that conviction, the city still fell.
The Khitan's forces were too strong, their numbers too overwhelming. Despite his relentless efforts, the Ding nation was lost.

On the day Ye Wanshan ordered his troops to retreat, the truth settled heavily upon him: one man alone could not defend a nation or reclaim what had been lost. He could only wait for the reinforcements of the imperial army to march north alongside him.
And so, he waited for thirteen long years. Thirteen years of suffering, of torment that never ceased, only to be broken by the rhythm of his sword swings. With each strike, his resolve grew harder.
At long last, the opportunity he had been waiting for arrived: Emperor Shizong's northern expedition.

Donning his well-maintained armor once again, he rallied his Tigers in Chains and stood at the city walls, awaiting the main forces.
But to his shock, the northern expedition was called off midway.

How could this happen? 
How could they just abandon the campaign?
His wife, daughter, and son were gone, and the people of the border city had suffered for far too long, yet the expedition was halted. How could they stop?
It was unacceptable. If the cowards hiding in the rear wouldn't march north, Ye Wanshan would lead them himself.

He turned his horse, his blade now aimed not at the enemy but at the very citizens of the city. A thick black cloud blotted out the sun, and in that heavy, oppressive silence, his face remained unreadable. 
He had made up his mind: If sacrificing the lives of a city's people could restore peace, then so be it.
That night, no enemies came to the gates. Yet, someone saw the Khitan entering the city, and the cries of agony echoed through the city where Ye Wanshan had lived for thirteen years.
His iron resolve, once full of care, now turned cold and callous.

Later, retreating to the Qinghe Buddhist Temple in search of some semblance of peace, Ye Wanshan encountered a monk who spoke of crossing the Bodhi Sea of suffering to reach the blissful shore.
But he knows the truth: This sea of suffering is too vast, too deep, and he can never cross it.

zh:
【众生·三】

【文士】

宣州谢朓楼饯别校书叔云
李白
弃我去者，昨日之日不可留。
乱我心者，今日之日多烦忧。
长风万里送秋雁，对此可以酣高楼。
蓬莱文章建安骨，中间小谢又清发。
俱怀逸兴壮思飞，欲上青天览明月。
抽刀断水水更流，举杯销愁愁更愁。
人生在世不称意，明朝散发弄扁舟。

江上吟
李白
木兰之枻沙棠舟，玉箫金管坐两头。
美酒樽中置千斛，载妓随波任去留。
仙人有待乘黄鹤，海客无心随白鸥。
屈平词赋悬日月，楚王台榭空山丘。
兴酣落笔摇五岳，诗成笑傲凌沧洲。
功名富贵若长在，汉水亦应西北流。

饮中八仙歌
杜甫
知章骑马似乘船，眼花落井水底眠。
汝阳三斗始朝天，道逢麴车口流涎，恨不移封向酒泉。
左相日兴费万钱，饮如长鲸吸百川，衔杯乐圣称避贤。
宗之潇洒美少年，举觞白眼望青天，皎如玉树临风前。
苏晋长斋绣佛前，醉中往往爱逃禅。
李白一斗诗百篇，长安市上酒家眠，天子呼来不上船，自称臣是酒中仙。
张旭三杯草圣传，脱帽露顶王公前，挥毫落纸如云烟。
焦遂五斗方卓然，高谈雄辩惊四筵。

天末怀李白
杜甫
凉风起天末，君子意如何。
鸿雁几时到，江湖秋水多。
文章憎命达，魑魅喜人过。
应共冤魂语，投诗赠汨罗。

江上值水如海势聊短述
杜甫
为人性僻耽佳句，语不惊人死不休。
老去诗篇浑漫兴，春来花鸟莫深愁。
新添水槛供垂钓，故著浮槎替入舟。
焉得思如陶谢手，令渠述作与同游。

【军旅】

从军行
杨炯
烽火照西京，心中自不平。
牙璋辞凤阙，铁骑绕龙城。
雪暗凋旗画，风多杂鼓声。
宁为百夫长，胜作一书生。

出塞二首·其一
王昌龄
秦时明月汉时关，万里长征人未还。
但使龙城飞将在，不教胡马度阴山。

燕歌行
高适
汉家烟尘在东北，汉将辞家破残贼。
男儿本自重横行，天子非常赐颜色。
摐金伐鼓下榆关，旌旆逶迤碣石间。
校尉羽书飞瀚海，单于猎火照狼山。
山川萧条极边土，胡骑凭陵杂风雨。
战士军前半死生，美人帐下犹歌舞。
大漠穷秋塞草腓，孤城落日斗兵稀。
身当恩遇恒轻敌，力尽关山未解围。
铁衣远戍辛勤久，玉箸应啼别离后。
少妇城南欲断肠，征人蓟北空回首。
边庭飘飖那可度，绝域苍茫更何有。
杀气三时作阵云，寒声一夜传刁斗。
相看白刃血纷纷，死节从来岂顾勋。
君不见沙场征战苦，至今犹忆李将军。

凉州词二首·其一
王翰
葡萄美酒夜光杯，欲饮琵琶马上催。
醉卧沙场君莫笑，古来征战几人回。
en:
【All Beings · III】 【The Literati】 Farewell to Uncle Yun, Imperial Librarian, at Xietiao Villa in Xuanzhou Li Bai What left me yesterday can no longer be detained; What worries me today is a long, long dreary day. In autumn wind for miles and miles wild geese fly high; Let us drink to our hearts' content in the tower high! The writings of the prince are instinct with power and grace, And my own poems are also well known in this place. Both of us have an ideal high; We would ascend the blue sky to catch the moon bright. But when we cut water with sword, still it will flow; We drink to drown our sorrow, but it won't go. Since we cannot fulfill our wish in this world of man, Why not sail in a boat with loosened hair? Let's plan! A Song on the River Li Bai In magnolia boat with sandalwood oars, At both ends flutes of jade and golden pipes play. In flagons of fine wine a thousand gallons stored, With singing girls we let the boat drift down the way. Immortals wait for yellow cranes to ride the air; Seamen are free to follow white gulls without care. Qu Yuan's songs hang with the sun and moon on high; King of Chu's bowers are but ruins neath the sky. Drunk, I wield my writing brush with might and main, My verse done, I laugh at the sea in disdain. If rank and wealth could last forever, as of old, The northwestward River Han would backward roll. Song of the Eight Immortal Drinkers Du Fu He Zhizhang rides his horse as in a boat he sways; He falls asleep in well when wine dims his eyes' gaze. Prince Ruyang must drink three gallons before he goes
To audience with the emperor; he'd slake his thirst
With wine from a wine-cart he meets; he'd fain immerse
His fief in Wine Spring, so that he might drink his fill. The left minister spends ten thousand coins each day; He drinks like a whale sucking rivers dry, they say. Cui Zongzhi is a handsome and a smart young man; He lifts to the blue sky his cup with white eyes, then
He stands, a jade tree before wind, in drunken way. Su Jin, a long-time faster before Buddha's shrine, Drunk, often loves to flee from the divine. Li Bai can write a hundred poems after drinking a gallon of wine;
He sleeps in a tavern of the capital fine. Summoned by the emperor, he won't take the order, But calls himself the drinker immortal, a grander. Zhang Xu, after three cups, writes cursive hand, the best; Hatless before the princes, he will stand, And wield his pen to make clouds o'er the land. Jiao Sui, after five gallons, begins to show his worth; His high talk and eloquent speech surprise the earth. Thinking of Li Bai at World's End Du Fu From the world's end cold wind begins to blow. What does my friend think now, do you know? When will wild geese bring me your word? The rivers and lakes are with autumn stirred. Fame is what literature disdains; Evil spirits delight in men's pains. You should have words with the poet drowned, And throw a poem into River Miluo profound. Short Lines on the River's Sea-like Sight Du Fu I'm never tired of seeking startling lines; I would not stop unless my words surprise. Old, I let my verse follow my heart's wish; In spring I'm free from flowers' and birds' grief. I've just added a rail to fish with ease; I've made a raft to take the place of boat. How I wish I could write as poets Tao and Xie, And travel with them in verse high and low! 【The Military】 Joining the Army Yang Jiong Beacon fires spread to the capital; My heart can't be calmed down at all. We leave the Palace, armed with tally; Our armored steeds besiege the vale. Snow darkens banners with paintings bright; Wind mingles with drums in the fight. I'd rather fight as a centurion
Than pore over books in the mansion. On the Frontier (I) Wang Changling The moon still shines on mountain passes as of yore. How many guardsmen of the Great Wall are no more! If the flying general were still there in command, No hostile steeds would have dared to invade our land. Song of the Northern Frontier Gao Shi War dusts spread northeast borderland; Our general, leaving home, fought the foe hand in hand. Men should go to the battlefield to win renown; Our emperor gave you favor with a golden crown. To the drumbeat we went through the pass, flags on the wane, Winding from fortress to fortress to the desert plain. Imperial orders sped over the Sea of Sand; The Tartar chief's hunting fires lit up Mount Wolf grand. Desolate and drear for miles and miles the border lay; The foe, like wind and rain, came, hoofs trampling the way. Half of our warriors lie dead on the battleground, While pretty girls sing and dance in the camp's merry round. The desert's dreary, grass withered at the end of fall; At sunset few men guard the lonely city wall. Though favored by the imperial grace, you're light of the foe; Despite all hardships, you can't break the siege, laid low. In armor long we've served in far-off land; In vain our wives have wept at home, wringing their hand. The southern city's young wives are broken-hearted; Their husbands at the northern frontier look southward, departed. The borderland is in a turmoil, who can foretell? Beyond the vast desert there is nothing but hell. All day along we see but slaughter and hear but blows; All night long we hear but the watchmen's bugle blows. Seeing each other's swords stained with blood, we would fight
And die for our country on the battleground, not for fame bright. Don't you know the bitterness of fighting with the foe? We still remember General Li who fought long ago. Song of Liangzhou (I) Wang Han With wine of grapes the cups of jade would glow at night; Drinking to pipa songs, we are summoned to fight. Don't laugh if we lay drunken on the battleground! How many warriors ever came back safe and sound?

衡州粮市，自本月以来，米价暗踊，斗米由百五十文骤至二百二十文，犹有市无粮。细察之，有牙侩承某府之托，以高市价一成之直，遍籴米麦，不问成色，尽数收纳。粮船络绎，自潭、朗、岳诸州溯湘江而下，夜半抵岸，米袋皆不署号，乡人不察，莫有异之。

又筋角、牛皮、桐油之属，一时并出。往日此物牙行冷淡，今索之甚急，价倍于常，犹供不应求。有潭州皮商李七郎者，满载牛皮二十车赴衡州，三日内竟罄。

en:
Jingnan Circuit Secret Report Summary
...
Over in Nanping, ever since Zhou Xingfeng fell deathly ill, only his young son Baoquan and a couple of generals have been at his bedside. Zhang Wenbiao, the Prefect of Hengzhou, might be stationed far away, but he keeps sending envoys bearing rare medicines to check on him.
...
The grain market prices in Hengzhou have been rising sharply this month. Rice prices quietly spiked from 150 to 220 coins a measure, and it's still sold out everywhere. We looked closer and found brokers hired by a certain estate buying up all the rice and wheat at a premium, no matter the quality. Endless grain boats are coming down the Xiang River from Tanzhou, Langzhou, and Yuezhou, docking in the dead of night. None of the sacks are marked, so the locals haven't noticed anything suspicious.

Also, military supplies like sinew, horn, cowhide, and tung oil are flying off the shelves. These used to sit gathering dust in the tradehalls, but now everyone wants them. Prices have doubled, and there's still not enough. A fur trader from Tanzhou named Li Qilang, brought 20 carts of cowhide to Hengzhou and sold out in three days.
Your disciple has personally verified these truths and recorded them for your eyes. Any further developments will be reported immediately.

The moment an honored guest sits down, summon everyone: kitchen hands, accountant, shopkeeper. Gather around the table, bang the drums, clash the gongs, and sing your blessings at full volume!

zh:
鼯之为鼠，食烟栖林。载飞载乳，乍兽乍禽。

飞鼠又称鼯鼠。关于鼯鼠的记载，在战国时所著的《荀子》中便有了。其《劝学篇》提到“鼯鼠五技而穷”，意思是鼯鼠能飞不能上屋，能缘不能穷木，能游不能渡谷，能穴不能掩身，能走不能先人，后来简化为“梧鼠技穷”，比喻一个人才能有限，仅有的一点本领已经使尽，再也没有别的办法了，世人多以此为典故。但魏晋时期的郭璞却另辟蹊径，作一《鼯鼠赞》说它以烟雾为食，栖息在森林之中，仿若是个不食人间烟火的小仙家啊。
en:
The flying squirrel eats mist and dwells in the forest. It flies and nurses, appearing as both beast and bird.

The flying squirrel is mentioned in the Xunzi from the Warring States period. The "Encouraging Learning" chapter mentions its five limited skills: it can fly but not onto a roof, climb but not to the top, swim but not across a valley, burrow but not hide its body, and run but not outpace a man. This led to the idiom "The flying squirrel's skills are exhausted," meaning someone has reached the limit of their meager talents. However, Guo Pu of the Wei and Jin periods took a different view, praising it as a little immortal that lives on mist and dwells in the forest, untainted by the world.

【工匠】

割飞二刀子歌

我家有剪刀，人云鬼国铁。

南中匠人淳用钢，再令盘屈随手伤。

两条神物秋冰薄，刃淬初蟾鞘金错。
越戟吴钩不足夸，斩犀切玉应怀怍。

神惊魄悸却收得，刃头已吐微微烟。

杨生青花紫石砚歌

佣刓抱水含满唇，暗洒苌弘冷血痕。
纱帷昼暖墨花春，轻沤漂沫松麝薰。
干腻薄重立脚匀，数寸光秋无日昏。
圆毫促点声静新，孔砚宽顽何足云。

绣
罗隐
一片丝罗轻似水，洞房西室女工劳。
花随玉指添春色，鸟逐金针长羽毛。
蜀锦谩夸声自贵，越绫虚说价功高。

【侠客】

游侠篇

洛阳丽春色，游侠骋轻肥。
水逐车轮转，尘随马足飞。
云影遥临盖，花气近薰衣。
东郊斗鸡罢，南皮射雉归。

送郑少府入辽共赋侠客远从戎

还家行且猎，弓矢速如飞。
地迥鹰犬疾，草深狐兔肥。
腰间带两绶，转盼生光辉。
顾谓今日战，何如随建威。

少年行四首·其一

新丰美酒斗十千，咸阳游侠多少年。

少年行四首·其二

出身仕汉羽林郎，初随骠骑战渔阳。

侠客行

赵客缦胡缨，吴钩霜雪明。
银鞍照白马，飒沓如流星。
十步杀一人，千里不留行。
事了拂衣去，深藏身与名。
闲过信陵饮，脱剑膝前横。
将炙啖朱亥，持觞劝侯嬴。
三杯吐然诺，五岳倒为轻。
眼花耳热后，意气素霓生。
救赵挥金槌，邯郸先震惊。
千秋二壮士，烜赫大梁城。
纵死侠骨香，不惭世上英。
谁能书阁下，白首太玄经。
en:
【All Beings · II】

【Artisan】

Song of the Two Flying Blades
Lu Lun
In my home, there is a pair of scissors, said to be forged of ghostly iron.
They cut silk and satin without dulling, yet after three years of use, one blade snapped.
A southern craftsman tempered them with steel, but the reforging left them brittle and flawed.
Remade into two flying blades, their gleam rivals clear snow, their edge holds frost.
Two divine objects, thin as autumn ice, the blades quenched like the new moon, sheaths inlaid with gold.
Yue halberds and Wu hooks are not worth boasting; these can slice rhino hide and cut jade, putting others to shame.
Once tested by the Han River's side, they trembled in the palm with a chilling sound.
Startled souls and fearful spirits were captured, as faint smoke rose from the blade's tip.
O blades, O blades, how brilliantly you shine, forcing demons to hide and monsters to cower.
Were it not for the master craftsman who transformed you, you'd lie forgotten in a tailor's box.

Song of the Purple Inkstone with Blue Patterns for Scholar Yang
Li He
The stoneworkers of Duanzhou are divinely skilled, treading the sky to grind knives and cut purple clouds.
Carved and hollowed to hold water full to the lip, secretly stained with Chang Hong's cold blood traces.
In warm daylight behind gauze curtains, ink blossoms like spring; light bubbles and floating froth carry pine and musk fragrance.
Dry, smooth, thin, or thick, it stands firm and even; inches of autumn radiance without a hint of dusk.
The round tip, pressed swiftly, makes a quiet, fresh sound; how can the broad, clumsy Kong inkstone compare?

Embroidery
Luo Yin
A piece of silk gauze light as water, in the inner chamber's west room, the maiden toils.
Flowers bloom beneath her jade fingers, adding spring hues; birds take shape chased by her golden needle, growing feathers.
Shu brocade may boast of its prized fame in vain; Yue silk vainly claims high worth and skill.
Fit to be made into a mandarin duck quilt, red leaves on branches do not hinder the needle's work.

【Knight-Errant】

The Wandering Knight
Chen Ziliang
Luoyang's beautiful spring scenery, where knights-errant ride sleek horses in splendor.
Water chases turning carriage wheels, dust flies with horses' hooves.
Cloud shadows approach from afar like canopies, floral scents near perfume their garments.
After cockfights in the eastern suburbs, they return from shooting pheasants at Nanpi.
At dusk on the river bridge, they raise their whips, cherishing the fading light.

Seeing Off Junior Official Zheng to Liaodong, We Compose on the Knight-Errant Going Far to Join the Army
Luo Binwang
Border beacon fires alarm the Elm Pass; the knight-errant crosses the Sanggan River.
Willow leaves split by silver arrowheads, peach blossoms shine upon jade saddles.
The full moon nears the bow's shadow, a line of stars enters the sword's tip.
Not like Prince Dan's retainers, who sang vainly of the cold Yishui waters.

On the Ancient Knight-Errant, Presented to the Generals in the Army
Cui Hao
In youth, bearing boldness and courage, fond of valor and knowing opportunity.
Taking up his sword, he leaves his gate, finding the lone city surrounded.
He kills men by the Liao River, rides back to Yuyang.
His golden chainmail lies scattered, his sable and rat fur robe is disheveled.
Returning home, he hunts as he travels, bow and arrows swift as flight.
The land vast, hawks and hounds are swift; grass deep, foxes and hares grow fat.
At his waist hang two silk ribbons, his glance shifting radiates brilliance.
Looking back, he asks of today's battle: how does it compare to following Jianwei?

Four Poems on Youthful Knights · I
Wang Wei
Xinfeng's fine wine costs ten thousand per dipper; in Xianyang, many youths are knights-errant.
Meeting, their spirited hearts drink to you, tying their horses by tall buildings under weeping willows.

Four Poems on Youthful Knights · II
Wang Wei
He began service as a Han Imperial Guard, first followed the Swift General to battle in Yuyang.
Who knows not the hardship of frontier posts? Even in death, the fragrance of a knight's bones remains.

The Song of the Knight-Errant
Li Bai
The knight of Zhao wears a rustic cap-strings, his Wu hook gleams with frost and snow.
Silver saddle shines on white steed, swift and fleet as a shooting star.
Ten paces, he slays one man; a thousand miles, he leaves no trace.
Deed done, he brushes off his clothes and departs, deep hiding his person and name.
Leisurely, he visits the Lord of Xinling to drink, lays his sword across his knees.
He offers roasted meat to Zhu Hai, raises the cup to urge Hou Ying.
Three cups, he utters a solemn pledge, lighter to him than the Five Peaks overturned.
Eyes dazzled, ears heated, afterward, his spirit rises like a white rainbow.
To save Zhao, he wielded the golden hammer, Handan was first shaken with awe.
Two heroes for a thousand autumns, their glory illuminated Daliang city.
Even in death, a knight's bones are fragrant, not shamed before the world's heroes.
Who can, in the scholar's tower, with white hair, pore over the "Tai Xuan Jing"?

非性别相关的外观道具：性别无关的外观道具（武器、武学特效、坐骑、摆件等） 不受转换性别影响。
保留原性别外观数据：转换性别后将保留原来性别的外观数据，玩家以后再次转换性别则可以直接使用原性别外观数据。
首次转换性别后可在7天内重置：首次转换性别后的7天内，可以免费重置转换性别效果，重置转换性别不会退还道具“阴阳易形丹”。同时会收回尚未使用的限时染色道具。
性别转换完成后，将会向好友发送外观转换私聊通知消息
en:
Battle and Social Data: After the body swap, the following information remains unchanged: Level, Attributes, Abilities, Inner Way, Profession, Sect, Guild, Social relationships, etc.
Gallery of Faces & Style Showcase: Uploaded Gallery data will be preserved. Personal Style Showcase will preserve the corresponding outfit and pose based on the selected appearance.
Outfit Presets: Presets from your original body type will be saved. However, after your body swap, outfit presets will not carry over and must be rearranged.
Appearance & Account Data: Upon the body swap, your character's model, voice, and other visuals will automatically adjust to match the new body type (you will be granted one chance to customize your face). All unlocked hero titles, explorations, and story quests will remain unchanged.
Non-wearable Cosmetic Items: Items not tied to body types (such as weapons, martial arts effects, mounts, and ornaments) are unaffected by the swap.
Preserve Data of the Original Body Type: After the body swap, your character's previous body type data will be preserved. If you swap back in the future, you can reuse the original appearance settings.
One-Time Reset Within 7 Days: You can undo the swap for free within 7 days after the first body swap. Resetting will not refund the item Yin Yang Morphing Pill, and any unused limited-time dye items will be reclaimed.
After the body swap, a private message will be sent to your friends to notify them of your new body type.

凡人之所以为人者，礼义也。礼义之始，在于正容体、齐颜色、顺辞令。容体正，颜色齐，辞令顺，而后礼义备。以正君臣、亲父子、和长幼。君臣正，父子亲，长幼和，而后礼义立。故冠而后服备，服备而后容体正、颜色齐、辞令顺。故曰：冠者，礼之始也。是故古者圣王重冠。

en:
【Meaning of the Capping Ceremony, Section 43】

What makes a person human is ritual propriety and righteousness. The foundation of ritual propriety and righteousness lies in correcting one's appearance and demeanor, harmonizing one's countenance, and aligning one's speech. When appearance and demeanor are correct, countenance is harmonious, and speech is aligned, then ritual propriety and righteousness are complete. This serves to rectify the relationship between ruler and minister, to foster affection between father and son, and to bring harmony between elder and younger. When ruler and minister are rectified, father and son are affectionate, and elder and younger are harmonious, then ritual propriety and righteousness are established. Therefore, only after the capping ceremony can one's attire be complete; only after attire is complete can one's appearance and demeanor be correct, countenance be harmonious, and speech be aligned. Hence it is said: The capping ceremony is the beginning of ritual propriety. For this reason, the sage kings of antiquity placed great importance on the capping ceremony.
In ancient times, the capping ceremony involved divining the day and the guest, to show reverence for the capping affair; reverence for the capping affair was to emphasize ritual propriety; emphasizing ritual propriety was to establish the foundation of the state.
……

zh:
庞妙的好学，是他最大的缺点。
也许是从小被私塾先生教坏了，庞妙所学甚杂。上至天文术法，下至木工织布，凡是他看到的有意思之物，都想学学。
庞妙说，人生苦短，不多经历些，怎么能算活了一次呢。因此，凡是他见到的技艺精湛之人，他都要喊声师傅。
有些人面子薄，架不住庞妙的拳拳热情，便应承下来。可教了几天，庞妙就被另外的事吸引，这位师傅的课程就都在一边。不过，庞妙却也不是那无理之人。他会备上酒水礼物，行个辞师礼，言辞恳切的态度让师傅也难以苛责，只得作罢。
一来二去，庞妙没学成什么手艺，辞师礼倒是搭进去不少。
可庞妙却觉得乐在其中。
都说名师要“桃李满天下”，那名徒不也应该“名师满天下”么。
何况，这么多个师傅，总有用到的那天。
en:
Pang Miao's eagerness to learn was his greatest flaw. 
Perhaps ruined by his childhood tutor, Pang Miao's studies were wildly varied. From astronomy and magic down to carpentry and weaving, anything interesting he saw, he wanted to learn. 
Pang Miao said life was short. If you didn't experience more, how could you say you had lived? Therefore, anyone he met with skilled craftsmanship, he would call Master.
Some people were thin-skinned and couldn't withstand Pang Miao's sincere enthusiasm, so they agreed. But after teaching for a few days, Pang Miao would be attracted to something else, and this master's lessons would be set aside. However, Pang Miao wasn't unreasonable. He would prepare wine and gifts and perform a ceremony to formally end the apprenticeship. His sincere attitude made it hard for the master to be harsh, so they would let it go.
After several rounds, Pang Miao didn't master any skills, but he spent a lot on farewell gifts. 
Yet Pang Miao felt joy in it.
They say a famous teacher should have "peaches and plums all under heaven." Shouldn't a famous disciple also have "masters all under heaven"? 
Besides, with so many masters, there would surely come a day when they'd be useful.
Song Daoyu

zh:
横江吾徒鉴之：

淮深归葬凉州，与万千归义英魂同饮霜雪。尘障已破，执念俱消。今为师弥留之际，留此铁血二誓：
其一：狂澜一门，誓与庙堂绝涉。自今而后，鹰扬不奉诏，龙战岂承恩！
其二：狂澜弟子，死后不留金玉满堂，不留青史虚名，不留残骨累世，酒葫满盛米油酒，黄泉路上无冻馁。
若见腰悬“一葫不归”之客，务必以礼相待。此子侠肝义胆，颇有我狂澜风骨，若愿共饮，当归入门下。
诀矣，珍重。
en:
To my disciple:

Let my bones be interred in Liangzhou, to share the eternal frost with the myriad righteous spirits gathered there. The mortal veil is torn, and my worldly obsessions have vanished. As I lie dying, I leave for our clan two vows, sworn in iron and blood.

The First Vow: The sect of Raging Tides will cut all ties with the throne. From this day on, our eagles answer no summons, and our dragons seek no grace!

The Second Vow: Our disciples shall not pass from this world leaving fortunes, false glory, or even their bones to trouble the living. Their gourds shall be full of rice, oil, and wine, to ensure no soul goes hungry or cold on the journey beyond.

Should you encounter one who wears the "Gourd of Remembrance," show him honor. That man possesses a hero's heart and our Raging Tides spirit. If he is willing to drink with you, welcome him into our fold.

Farewell, and be well.

zh: 《阳关三叠》，中国古曲，又名《阳关曲》、《渭城曲》。该曲取材自《送元二使安西》：“渭城朝雨浥轻尘，客舍青青柳色新。劝君更尽一杯酒，西出阳关无故人”。唐时该曲被编成琴歌，歌曲分三大段，叠唱原诗外，加入由原诗诗意所发展的若干词句，为当时的乐工广为传唱。诗中“西出阳关无故人”一反复吟唱三遍，故名《阳关三叠》。
en: Three Steps of Yangguan (also known as Yangguan Tune or Weicheng Tune) is a traditional Chinese piece, adapted from A Farewell Song to Yuan'er by Wang Wei: "No dust is raised on the road wet with morning rain. The willows by the hotel look so fresh and green. I invite you to drink a cup of wine again. The Yangguan Pass, no more friends will be seen." During the Tang Dynasty, this piece was arranged as a Guqin song, consisting of three main sections. In addition to repeatedly singing the original verses, several new lines were added, expanding on the imagery of the poem. The line "The Yangguan Pass, no more friends will be seen" is sung three times, which led to the name Three Steps of Yangguan.

zh:
也不知这信，最后会落到谁手上。
是丁香这臭丫头？还是小棠那妻管严？
没想到吧？这次老子要跟将军去干一场大事！就我一个，没带你们！
可惜了，不能亲眼瞧见你们那副吃瘪的样儿。
你们总笑我胆小怕死。可你们不懂，只有怕死的人，鼻子才尖，能闻见危险的味儿。这次，我就闻着了——将军不对劲。
放心，我钱多多不是去送死，是去“活”将军的命。也只有我这种把命看得比钱还金贵的人，才晓得怎么给将军蹚出一条活路，对吧？
不过……话是这么说，万一呢？
若真回不来了，我可不能背上“人死了钱没花完”的千古恶名。我那些心肝宝贝的去处，都写在咱们那面破旗子上了。那些钱，也算我给它们找了个好归宿，你们……就替我办妥了吧。
唉，不写了！越写心越疼！我钱多多精明一辈子，这次肯定能活着回来，还要把将军囫囵个儿地带回来！等着给我摆庆功宴吧！
en:
No knowing whose hands this letter will end up in.
That little brat Ding Xiang's? Or Xiaotang's, that henpecked fool's?
Did not see this coming, did you? This time I am going off with the General to do something truly great, and I am not taking either of you along.
What a pity. I will not get to see the looks on your faces when you choke on it.
You are always laughing at me for being timid, for fearing death. But you do not understand. Only a man who fears death has the nose to smell danger. And this time, I smelled it. Something is wrong with the General.
Do not worry. I, Qian Duoduo, am not going to throw my life away. I am going to keep the General alive. Only a man like me, who prizes his life even more than silver, knows how to carve out a road back from death. Is that not so?
Still... for all that, what if?
If I truly do not make it back, I cannot very well go down with the name of a man who died without spending his money. The whereabouts of all my precious things are written on that ragged old banner of ours. You two... take care of it for me. At least let the money end up somewhere decent.
Bah, enough of this. The more I write, the more my heart aches. I have been shrewd all my life. This time too, I will surely come back alive, and bring the General back whole as well. So wait for me, and make ready the victory feast.
Gu Wenyun
Xiao Lin Nuo Ji You

在那未遭饥荒的太平岁月，达安郑氏显赫非常，郑氏夫妻宅心仁厚，广结善缘，惠及无数邻里，众人皆怀敬仰之心。
后来，小少爷郑鄂诞生。众人皆无限喜悦，四方宾朋，皆以贺礼相赠。而其中尤为珍贵的，便是祖母亲手做的金丝长命缕。寓意人生圆满，长命百岁。这也是众人共同的期盼。
彼时岁月，和谐美满，恍若天伦齐聚，令人深信此情此景，将永恒延续。
流寇之乱后，郑鄂立于废墟之上，眼睁睁的看着阿阮死在自己面前，家破人亡。昔日团圆美满，而今只剩他一人。呵，团团圆圆，倒是把自己落下了……长命百岁，只有郑鄂一个人的长命……要这百岁又如何呢？
郑鄂解下那承载着众人期望的长命缕，轻置于阿阮墓前。最愿长命之人已逝，自己的命，呵……便也留在这边吧。
en:
In the peaceful years before famine struck, the Zheng family of Da'an stood in great prestige. Kind and generous, the Zheng couple earned the respect of all, aiding neighbors and forging goodwill throughout the community.
Then came the birth of young master Zheng E. The whole town rejoiced—guests from far and wide arrived with gifts, the most precious among them a Gilded Longevity Thread handwoven by his grandmother, symbolizing a full life and a wish for a hundred years of peace and joy. Everyone shared that hope.
Those days were warm and bright, filled with harmony and family. It felt as if such happiness would last forever.
But after the chaos of marauders, Zheng E stood alone in the ruins, watching A'Ruan die before his eyes. His home gone, his family lost. Once surrounded by love, now he was the only one left. Reunion? What a cruel joke. Longevity? Only he had lived.
He untied the golden thread, once a symbol of everyone's hopes, and placed it gently on A'Ruan's grave. The one most wished to live long was gone. As for his own life... he left it there too.

十六巷在持续监测使用第三方辅助软件的行为，除加大对举报投诉对象审查外，也在技术上采取各项措施不断完善游戏内的异常行为校验功能，核实为违规的账号将进行严厉打击，以维护江湖的公平公正。

违规行为包括但不限于：使用外挂、加速类软件、或其他破坏游戏公平性的软件及"坐挂车"行为。针对「止戈」 等玩法场景，依据具体违规情况，对账号进行清除所有排行榜成绩、相关玩法禁赛、暂时禁止登录、永久禁止登录等处罚；针对「百业战」场景，十六巷也将加严核查封禁力度，并对恶意利用成员开挂获利的百业进行包括但不限于负扣胜场，降级，禁赛等处罚。
en:
Sixteen Lanes continuously monitors the use of third-party assist software. In addition to increasing scrutiny on reported subjects, we are implementing various technical measures to constantly improve the detection of abnormal behavior within the game. Accounts verified as violating rules will be strictly penalized to maintain fairness and justice in the Jianghu.

Violations include but are not limited to: use of cheats, speed hacks, or other software that undermines game fairness, as well as "getting carried by cheaters". For gameplay scenarios such as "Arena", penalties include wiping all leaderboard records, banning from relevant modes, temporary login bans, or permanent login bans, depending on the severity. For "Guild War" scenarios, Sixteen Lanes will also strictly increase verification and banning efforts. Guilds that maliciously profit from members using cheats will face penalties including, but not limited to, deduction of wins, demotion, and bans.

zh:
胡二饼是从一场地震中逃出来的。
随身的只有一只老狗，还有剩下的几块烤馕。
老狗不懂得什么叫流浪，它只知道和主人一起走。有主人，它就有家。
穿越沙海，路途茫茫，胡二饼把每一块馕都一分为二，一人一狗虽然吃不饱，但却也形影不离。
直到行囊空空，一人一狗又走了很远。
胡二饼因为饥渴昏倒在沙漠里。最后，他只看到老狗焦急地扒拉着他，随后狂吠着跑开。
走吧，老伙计。记得填饱肚子……

胡二饼是在坎尔孜里醒来的。
村民说，他们发现了一只中暑的老狗，躺在村口，耷拉舌头倒着气。见有人来，它拼了命站起来，拽着人的裤脚往沙漠里走，却摇摇晃晃地再摔倒。人们顺着方向走，发现了昏倒在沙漠里的胡二饼。
胡二饼问，那老狗呢。
村里人沉默着，带着胡二饼来到凉棚下。老狗见胡二饼来了，用尽最后一点力气抬起头，摇着尾巴哈气。
那一天，胡二饼陪着老狗说了好多话，直到老狗的尾巴轻轻耷拉，再也不动了。
胡二饼很自责，最后也没让老狗吃饱了再走。
en:
Hu Erbing escaped from an earthquake. 
All he had with him was an old dog and a few remaining pieces of baked naan. 
The old dog didn't understand what wandering meant. It only knew to walk with its master. Where the master was, there was home. 
Crossing the sea of sand, the road was endless. Hu Erbing divided each piece of naan in two. Though man and dog weren't full, they were inseparable. 
Until the pack was empty, and man and dog had walked a long way further. 
Hu Erbing collapsed in the desert from thirst and hunger. In the end, he only saw the old dog anxiously pawing at him, then barking wildly and running off. 
Go on, old friend. Remember to fill your belly... 

Hu Erbing woke up in Karez. 
The villagers said they had found an old dog suffering from heatstroke lying at the village entrance, tongue lolling, gasping for breath. Seeing people approach, it struggled to stand up, tugged at their pant legs trying to lead them into the desert, then wobbled and fell again. People followed the direction and found Hu Erbing unconscious in the desert. 
Hu Erbing asked, where was the old dog? 
The villagers were silent, leading Hu Erbing to a shaded shelter. Seeing Hu Erbing arrive, the old dog used its last bit of strength to lift its head, wagging its tail and panting. 
That day, Hu Erbing talked to the old dog for a long time, until the old dog's tail gently drooped and moved no more. 
Hu Erbing blamed himself. In the end, he hadn't even let the old dog leave on a full stomach.

At last, Dax found a kind-hearted owner. 
That day, as always, it went out to work and—of course—ended up breaking something. But instead of scolding it for its clumsy paws, the owner smiled warmly and called it a "good kitty." 
In that moment, Dax made a promise: it would repay this kindness every day. 
It cleaned the house, shared its favorite dried fish, and chased away pests. But the owner's bowl held tempting water—after a sip, Dax curled up on the owner's chest and peacefully fell asleep. 
Dax thought to itself: If only this owner were truly its own—one who would always let it rest anywhere it pleased. 
Dax was a lucky cat. Its wish would come true one day. 
From now on, the owner could rely on Dax.

zh:
【檀弓上第三】

公仪仲子之丧，檀弓免焉。仲子舍其孙而立其子。檀弓曰：何居？我未之前闻也。趋而就子服伯子于门右，曰：仲子舍其孙而立其子，何也？伯子曰：仲子亦犹行古之道也。昔者文王舍伯邑考而立武王，微子舍其孙腯而立衍也。夫仲子亦犹行古之道也。子游问诸孔子，孔子曰：否。立孙。
事亲有隐而无犯，左右就养无方，服勤至死，致丧三年。事君有犯而无隐，左右就养有方，服勤至死，方丧三年。事师无犯无隐，左右就养无方，服勤至死，心丧三年。
季武子成寝，杜氏之葬在西阶之下，请合葬焉，许之，入宫而不敢哭。武子曰：合葬，非古也，自周公以来，未之有改也。吾许其大而不许其细，何居？命之哭。
子上之母死而不丧，门人问诸子思曰：昔者子之先君子丧出母乎？曰：然。子之不使白也丧之，何也？子思曰：昔者吾先君子无所失道，道隆则从而隆，道污则从而污，伋则安能为伋也妻者，是为白也母；不为伋也妻者，是不为白也母，故孔氏之不丧出母，自子思始也。
孔子曰：拜而后稽颡，颓乎其顺也；稽颡而后拜，颀乎其至也，三年之丧，吾从其至者。
孔子既得合葬于防，曰：吾闻之，古也墓而不坟，今丘也，东西南北之人也，不可以弗识也，于是封之，崇四尺，孔子先反，门人后，雨甚至，孔子问焉，曰：尔来何迟也？曰：防墓崩。孔子不应三，孔子泫然流涕曰：吾闻之，古不修墓。
孔子哭子路于中庭，有人吊者，而夫子拜之，既哭，进使者而问故，使者曰：醢之矣，遂命复醢。
曾子曰：朋友之墓有宿草，而不哭焉。
子思曰：丧三日而殡，凡附于身者，必诚必信，勿之有悔焉耳矣三月而葬，凡附于棺者，必诚必信，勿之有悔焉耳矣。丧三年以为极亡则弗之忘矣故君子有终身之忧而无一朝之患，故忌日不乐。
孔子少孤，不知其墓，殡于五父之衢，人之见之者，皆以为葬也。其慎也，盖殡也，问于鄹曼父之母，然后得合葬于防。
邻有丧，舂不相；里有殡，不巷歌。丧冠不𮉫。
有虞氏瓦棺，夏后氏垐周，殷人棺椁，周人墙置翣，周人以殷人之棺椁葬长殇，以夏后氏之垐周葬中殇、下殇，以有虞氏之瓦棺葬无服之殇。
夏后氏尚黑，大事敛用昏，戎事乘骊，牲用玄。殷人尚白，大事敛用日中，戎事乘翰，牲用白。周人尚赤，大事敛用日出，戎事乘𫘪，牲用骍。
穆公之母卒，使人问于曾子曰：如之何？对曰：申也闻诸申之父曰：哭泣之哀，齐斩之情，𫗴粥之食，自天子达布幕，卫也；縿幕，鲁也。
晋献公将杀其世子申生，公子重耳谓之曰：子盖言子之志于公乎？世子曰：不可。君安骊姬，是我伤公之心也。曰：然则盖行乎？世子曰：不可。君谓我欲弑君也，天下岂有无父之国哉？吾何行如之？使人辞于狐突曰：申生有罪，不念伯氏之言也，以至于死，申生不敢爱其死。虽然，吾君老矣，子少，国家多难，伯氏不出而图吾君，伯氏苟出而图吾君，申生受赐而死。再拜稽首，乃卒。是以为恭世子也。
鲁人有朝祥而莫歌者，子路笑之。夫子曰：由，尔责于人，终无巳夫。三年之丧，亦巳久矣夫。子路出，夫子曰：又多乎哉？逾月则其善也。
鲁庄公及宋人战于乘丘，县贲父御，卜国为右。马惊，败绩，公队，佐车授绥。公曰：末之卜也。县贲父曰：他日不败绩，而今败绩，是无勇也。遂死之。圉人浴马，有流矢在白肉。公曰：非其罪也。遂诔之。士之有诔，自此始也。

en:
【Tan Gong I】

At the mourning rites for Gongyi Zhongzi, Tan Gong wore the mourning band of hemp. Zhongzi set aside his grandson and established his son as heir. Tan Gong said: "How is this? I have never heard of such a thing before." He hurried to Zifu Bozi, who stood on the right side of the gate, and said: "Zhongzi set aside his grandson and established his son as heir—why?" Bozi said: "Zhongzi is simply following the ancient way. In former times, King Wen set aside Bo Yikao and established King Wu; Weizi set aside his grandson Dun and established Yan. Thus Zhongzi is also following the ancient way." Ziyou asked Confucius about this, and Confucius said: "No. The grandson should be established."
In serving parents, one may conceal their faults but must not openly remonstrate against them; one attends to their needs without restriction, serving them diligently until death, and mourns for them with full mourning for three years. In serving a ruler, one may openly remonstrate but must not conceal faults; one attends to duties in an orderly manner, serving diligently until death, and mourns as if for a parent for three years. In serving a teacher, one neither openly remonstrates nor conceals faults; one attends without restriction, serving diligently until death, and mourns in one's heart for three years.
Ji Wuzi completed his bedchamber, and the Du family's burial was located beneath the western steps. They requested to be buried together with him, and he permitted it. They entered the house but dared not weep. Wuzi said: "Joint burial is not an ancient practice; since the Duke of Zhou, there has been no change to this. I permitted the great matter but not the small—how is this?" He ordered them to weep.
When Zishang's mother died, he did not observe mourning for her. His disciples asked Zisi: "In former times, did your late father mourn for his divorced mother?" He said: "Yes." "Then why do you not have Bai observe mourning for her?" Zisi said: "In former times, my late father never erred from the Way. When the Way flourished, he followed it in flourishing; when the Way declined, he followed it in declining. Ji—how could I? She who was the wife of Ji is the mother of Bai; she who is not the wife of Ji is not the mother of Bai. Therefore, the Kong family's not mourning for divorced mothers began with Zisi."
Confucius said: "To bow first and then knock the head to the ground—this is submissive and proper. To knock the head first and then bow—this is sincere and reverent. For the three-year mourning, I follow the sincere and reverent one."
After Confucius had obtained the joint burial at Fang, he said: "I have heard that in antiquity they made graves but did not raise mounds. But now I, Qiu, am a man of the four directions, and it would not do to have no marker." Thereupon he raised a mound four feet high. Confucius returned first, and his disciples came later. A heavy rain arrived, and Confucius asked them: "Why are you so late?" They said: "The grave mound at Fang collapsed." Confucius did not answer, and they said it three times. Confucius, shedding tears, said: "I have heard that in antiquity they did not repair graves."
Confucius wept for Zilu in the central courtyard. When someone came to offer condolences, the Master bowed to him. After the weeping, he summoned the messenger and asked about the circumstances. The messenger said: "He was made into mincemeat." Thereupon he ordered the mincemeat to be covered.
Zengzi said: "When a friend's grave has grass from the previous year, one no longer weeps for him."
Zisi said: "When mourning, after three days the body is encoffined. Everything that accompanies the body must be done with sincerity and faithfulness, so that there is no regret. After three months, the burial takes place. Everything that accompanies the coffin must be done with sincerity and faithfulness, so that there is no regret. Three years of mourning is considered the extreme limit, and after that one does not forget the deceased. Therefore the noble man has lifelong grief but no single day's calamity. Thus on the day of remembrance, he does not take pleasure."
Confucius was orphaned young and did not know his father's grave. His mother was encoffined at the thoroughfare of Wufu. Those who saw it all thought it was a burial. Because he was so careful, it was in fact an encoffining. He asked the mother of Zou Manfu, and only then was he able to obtain the joint burial at Fang.
When a neighbor has a mourning, one does not pound rice with a rhythmic song; when a village has an encoffining, one does not sing in the lane. The mourning cap is not adorned with a tassel.
The Yu clan used earthenware coffins; the Xia Hou clan surrounded them with bricks; the Yin people used inner and outer coffins; the Zhou people added walls and set up feather fans. The Zhou buried those who died young in their prime with the Yin people's inner and outer coffins, those who died in middle youth or lower youth with the Xia Hou clan's brick enclosure, and those who died before the age of mourning with the Yu clan's earthenware coffin.
The Xia Hou clan honored black. For major events, they performed the encoffining at dusk; for military affairs, they rode black horses; for sacrifices, they used black victims. The Yin people honored white. For major events, they performed the encoffining at midday; for military affairs, they rode white horses; for sacrifices, they used white victims. The Zhou people honored red. For major events, they performed the encoffining at sunrise; for military affairs, they rode red horses with white bellies; for sacrifices, they used red victims.
When Duke Mu's mother died, he sent someone to ask Zengzi: "What should be done?" He replied: "Shen has heard from his father: 'The grief of weeping and wailing, the feelings expressed in the unhemmed and hemmed mourning garments, the food of gruel and porridge—from the Son of Heaven down, all are the same. The plain cloth curtain is the custom of Wei; the silk curtain is the custom of Lu.'"
Duke Xian of Jin was about to kill his heir apparent, Shensheng. Gongzi Chong'er said to him: "Why do you not make your intentions known to the Duke?" The heir apparent said: "I cannot. The Duke is content with Li Ji—this would wound the Duke's heart." Chong'er said: "Then why not leave?" The heir apparent said: "I cannot. The Duke would say I intended to assassinate him. Is there any state in the world without a father? Where could I go?" He sent someone to bid farewell to Hutuo, saying: "Shensheng has committed an offense—he did not heed your words, and so has come to death. Shensheng does not dare to begrudge his death. Nevertheless, our lord is old, his son is young, and the state is beset with difficulties. If you do not come forth to plan for our lord, and if you do come forth to plan for our lord, Shensheng will receive your favor and die." He bowed twice and knocked his head to the ground, and then died. For this reason he was called the Reverent Heir Apparent.
A man of Lu sang in the evening after completing the mourning of one year. Zilu laughed at him. The Master said: "You, Qiu—your reproach of others never ends! The three-year mourning is already long enough." When Zilu left, the Master said: "How much longer was it? If he had waited another month, it would have been proper."
Duke Zhuang of Lu fought against the men of Song at Chengqiu. Xian Benfu drove the chariot, and Bu Guo served as the warrior on the right. The horses were startled, and the formation was broken. The Duke fell, and the assistant chariot handed him the reins. The Duke said: "I did not consult the divination beforehand." Xian Benfu said: "On other days we did not lose the battle, but today we lost—this is a lack of courage." Thereupon he died in the fight. When the groom bathed the horses, there was a stray arrow in the white flesh. The Duke said: "This was not his fault." Thereupon he composed a eulogy for him. The practice of composing eulogies for officers began from this time.

Records of Esoteric Buddhism state: offering the bones of the dead to the vultures in the Shmashana Grove is an act of great merit. If one possesses a mountain of white bones, is it not the perfect foundation to mold a Vajra body? Thus, the Vajra Art and the Shmashana Inner Art were created, serving as furnace and blood-leech to one another.
Once the Shmashana Inner Art is mastered, the victim becomes my cauldron, perishing as their marrow is drained. Watching their corpses curl like twisted branches, their wrathful faces blooming like flowers upon white bone, one knows the divine path is within reach!
Yet, one must remember: Shmashana is the soil, and Vajra is the seed. The root of Shmashana must never overpower the Vajra, lest master and servant reverse roles: should that happen, the one blooming upon the white bones will likely be myself!

Hangzhou Prefecture Secret Report Summary
...
Trade in the Wuyue region is going on as usual, and they're still paying their yearly tribute to Song. The people are at peace, with sufficient food and clothing. Goods like porcelain, silk, and tea are exported annually in exchange for northern horses, ginseng, and pelts.
Merchants flock here, but Song established border markets between Qingzhou and Xuzhou. The borders are heavily guarded and require an official writ to cross.
...
Foreign merchants gathered to plan a route through Qingzhou Port. They want to switch routes from land to sea and reach Hangzhou directly by water. If this works out, the trade route will open for unhindered sailing. Foreign merchants from Liao and Goryeo also wish to join the voyages.

Your disciple has personally verified these truths and recorded them for your eyes. Any further developments will be reported immediately.

“那是谁？你看见了谁？”
“是、是——”
“是那个魔头！哈哈哈，听啊，雷声，她出来了！杀了那个写字的，又杀了这个斗狠的！”
“然后杀了你……杀了你……杀了这一屋子的人——杀了满江湖！杀到长安去！一个不留……一个不留……哈哈哈哈……”
“一步杀一人，十步灭一门，旧鬼哭，新鬼笑，我渡冤魂到九霄……”
“不是我，呜不是我。是……是……”
“先把她关起来。”
“没有空屋子了，就关在她房里吧。”
“不是我，不是我，是她，是魔头……”
“犯人就得受罚，没人能在我眼前瞒住什么——”
en:
"Murong, you stand accused of murder. A life for a life."
"I didn't... I didn't kill him! It wasn't me. I swear it wasn't!"
"Who was it? Who did you see?"
"It was... it was..."
"The fiend! Hahaha! Hear that thunder? She's loose again! First she killed the scholar, now the warrior!"
"And then she'll kill you... And you... Everyone in this room! She'll kill the whole jianghu, all the way to Chang'an! She won't leave any alive... not one! Hahahaha!"
"One step, one corpse. Ten steps, a whole family. Old ghosts weep, new ghosts laugh! I send the wronged souls soaring to the heavens..."
"Not me... It wasn't me. It was... it was..."
"Lock her up for now."
"There are no empty rooms. Just lock her in her own room."
"It wasn't me. It wasn't me. It was her... the fiend..."
"Hmph. No crime goes unpunished. No one can hide the truth from me—"

zh:
昨日难得休息，本想偷闲出去走走，刚到湖边，就瞧见几个半大娃娃，卷着裤腿，正兴冲冲地往水里蹚，张罗着要寻什么宝贝。
那湖水看着清浅，实则往里几步便是陡崖，眼见他们越走越深，我到底没忍住，一个个给拎了回来。之后自是免不了挨家挨户送回去，一路上边走衣服边滴着水，山风一吹，透心凉。
得了，好好的假期，就这么泡汤了，我当真是个劳碌命啊……
回解忧司后，才发觉有些鼻塞头晕。唉，半点好处没捞着不说，倒是染了风寒。
我正裹着被子喝热水，那几个娃娃又探头探脑溜进院来，搁下一包药在门口，就像兔子似的跑了。那药熬出来苦得很，也不知道他们从哪找来的。
罢了罢了，横竖平日也无甚大案要办，就当活动筋骨了。
en:
I finally had a day off yesterday and was planning to take it easy with a walk by the lake. But the moment I got there, I saw a bunch of kids with their pant legs rolled up, wading eagerly into the water in search of some treasure.
The lake appeared shallow, but just a few steps in lay a steep drop. Seeing them wade deeper and deeper, I couldn't just stand by, so I hauled them back out one by one.
And of course, that meant walking each of them home afterward. Dripping wet along the way, I was chilled to the bone by the mountain wind.
Alas, my precious day off is ruined. I am truly destined for a life of toil...
By the time I got back to the Bureau of Relief, I was already feeling stuffed up and lightheaded. I gained nothing for my trouble but caught a chill instead.
While I was wrapped in a quilt, drinking hot water, those youths sneaked back into the courtyard. They left a packet of medicine at the door and bolted like frightened rabbits. The decoction was incredibly bitter; heaven knows where they found it.
Ah, well, let it be. There are no major cases to handle lately anyway. Might as well count it as exercise.

      天水集的大伙儿都会提起你，说你行侠仗义，我们听着都很开心，也惦记着你。你阿婶怕你在外面吃不饱穿不暖，时常念叨你呢。有时间就来摊子坐坐啊。
      对了，开烫菜摊子赚了些钱，我们想着也帮衬帮衬别人，就做了些饭菜送给了几个老伙计。怕他们觉得不好意思，我们几个就说，是你要给他们送的。他们还奇怪，说怎么会有没见过的好心人惦记他们呢。老张说这孩子就是这样的，是个热心肠的大侠！他们不太好意思，就给你写了字条，你一起看看吧。
      好了，不说了，待会要来客人了，就到这儿吧。
      希望你一个人在外吃饱穿暖，平平安安。

en:
Young Hero: 
Long time no see. How have you been? 
Thanks to you, the stall is doing great. Your Auntie hasn't been this happy in ages—she smiles, chatting with customers all day, and even dances a few steps when the Pipa lady plays! When it's slow, Old Zhang and Old Yao even try to race the lads from the deity competition team, haha. 
Everyone at Skybrim Market speaks of your chivalry. We are happy to hear it and miss you often. Your Auntie worries you aren't eating well or staying warm. She talks about you all the time. Come visit the stall when you can. 
Oh, we made some money from the scalding vegetable stall, so we thought we'd help others out. We sent some food to a few old partners. We were afraid they'd feel embarrassed, so we said it was from you. They were surprised a kind hero remembered them! Old Zhang said, "That child is just warm-hearted like that!" They were shy, so they wrote you notes. Take a look. 
Okay, customers are coming. I'll stop here. 
Stay warm, fed, and safe out there.

我头一回负责整晋升名单，费劲扒拉弄了半天，刚整的差不离，说去泡个汤泉醒醒脑子。结果在汤泉边张师兄他们几个非得闹我，撕吧了两下，把我名单弄掉水里了……名字全糊了。我费老鼻子劲才把人名一个个誊清楚。所以本来早该升的位子就这么让我给耽误了，还有弄错的，你看这事儿整的……
不过你放心，现在都收拾利整了！堂主吩咐了，该补的咱一样不少，全都补上。除了照常晋升，堂主还另外给添了点#Y长鸣玉#E和#Y江湖声望#E当赔礼，必不叫自家铁子吃亏。
这事儿是我办的不靠谱，你别往心里去。下回回山门，我请你喝酒！
en:
To my magnanimous Best Bro: 
I'm terribly sorry! It's all because I'm unreliable and messed up your promotion! 
It was my first time handling the promotion list. I worked on it for ages, finally got it about right, and went to the hot spring to clear my head. Then Brother Zhang and the guys started messing around, we tussled a bit, and the list fell into the water... the names got all smudged. I tried my hardest to copy them out clearly again. That's why the positions that should have been promoted ages ago got delayed, and some were even wrong. Look at this mess... 
But don't worry, it's all sorted now! The Hall Master ordered that we make up for everything. Besides the regular promotion, the Hall Master added some #YEcho Jade#E and #YJianghu Reputation#E as an apology. We won't let our own bro lose out. 
This was my screw-up, please don't take it to heart. Next time you're back at the gate, drinks are on me!

那时六六的主人死在了封龙书院，六六在家里几乎快饿死，恰逢荆老头到墨城送蜂蜜，这才把它救了回来。
然而，吃饱后的六六总是想着往山外跑，又总是饿晕了被荆老头带回来。荆老头知道它是在找它的主人，只是他再也回不来了。
如今十多年过去，六六也失去了以往的精力，再也无法跑出去。但也许用不了多久它就能见到它的主人了。

Sixty-Six was adopted by Old Man Jing.
His original owner had died at Dragonbend Academy. Sixty-Six was starving at home when Old Man Jing, delivering honey to Mohist City, found him and brought him back.
But after meals, Sixty-Six always tried to run out of the mountains. And always came back starving, carried by Old Man Jing. Jing knew that Sixty-Six was looking for his master. The master who would never return.
Now, over ten years have passed. Sixty-Six has lost his old energy. He can't run anymore.
But maybe, soon, he'll see his master again.

zh:
多年前的一日，徐尚浅刚刚收了班回来，就听见家里吵吵嚷嚷。
推开门，原来是几个邻居，在院子里讨个说法。
徐家的小儿子调皮，打碎了王家院里的茶罐，淹死了耿家刚出生的小鸡，又爬上张家的门墙，为了摘个柿子，摇摇晃晃竟弄掉不少。徐家娘子一个劲道歉赔不是。徐尚浅的额头开始隐隐作痛。
眼看着徐尚浅回来，一群邻居又叽叽喳喳围上来。
“我说徐四，你也不知道管管你家孩子！”
“小小年纪就杀生，以后还不得杀人放火啊！”
“我们家的柿子可是外地传来的，我自己都不舍得吃！”
此起彼伏的叫嚷，让徐尚浅的额头更痛。
“对不住，真对不住。我一定管束小儿。给各位添麻烦了，有多少损失，我赔，我赔……”
送走了邻居们，徐尚浅疲惫地低下头。
“孽障！还不过来……不对，你今天不应该去学堂么！”
话音未落，身后的敲门声再次响起。
一推开门，夫子拿着戒尺，怒气冲冲地站着。

“夫子您受累，我一定会好好说他。明天，我保证明天，我亲自送他去学堂，再不让他逃课了……”
“哼，朽木不可雕也！”夫子一甩袖子，冷哼一声离去。

徐尚浅几乎失去了所有的力气。他只想好好睡一觉。
他命儿子跪在院中抄书，不抄完不准睡。

躺在床上，徐尚浅还没喘过气，娘子便忧心忡忡地进来。
“阿爷来信，说家里的期契快到了，催我们赶紧寄点钱。你看咱们家，虽然还不至于揭不开锅，可实在也……”
徐尚浅只觉得头晕目眩。临了，他只得长叹一声。
“明天我去问问，书院里还有没有帮人抄书的活，多抄几份……”
耳边的娘子还在抱怨，可徐尚浅只觉得身坠青云，沉沉睡去。
en:
One day many years ago, just as Xu Shangqian had returned from his shift, he heard a clamor at home.
Pushing the door open, he found several neighbors in the courtyard demanding an explanation.
The Xu family's youngest son was mischievous. He had broken a tea jar in the Wang family's yard, drowning the Geng family's newly hatched chicks. Then he had climbed the Zhang family's gate wall to pick a persimmon and, swaying unsteadily, had knocked quite a few down. Lady Xu was apologizing profusely and offering compensation. A dull pain began throbbing in Xu Shangqian's forehead.
Seeing Xu Shangqian return, the group of neighbors swarmed around him again, chattering.
"I say, Fourth Brother Xu, don't you know how to control your child!"
"Killing living things at such a young age, he'll be murdering and setting fires when he grows up!"
"Our persimmons came from outside the region! I couldn't even bear to eat them myself!"
The rising and falling shouts made the pain in Xu Shangqian's forehead worse.
"My apologies, truly my apologies. I will definitely discipline my son. I've troubled you all. Whatever the losses are, I'll compensate, I'll compensate..."
After seeing off the neighbors, Xu Shangqian lowered his head wearily.
"You little troublemaker! Come here now... Wait, shouldn't you be at school today!"
Before the words had fully left his mouth, knocking sounded at the door again.
Opening it, the schoolmaster stood there, holding a ruler, furious.

"Master, you've been troubled. I will definitely speak to him sternly. Tomorrow, I promise tomorrow, I will personally take him to school. I won't let him skip class again..."
"Hmph! Rotten wood cannot be carved!" The master flicked his sleeve, snorted coldly, and left.

Xu Shangqian had almost lost all his strength. He just wanted to sleep.
He ordered his son to kneel in the courtyard and copy texts, forbidding him to sleep until he finished.

Lying in bed, before Xu Shangqian could even catch his breath, his wife came in, worried.
"Father wrote. The land lease at home is almost due, urging us to send some money quickly. Look at our family... we're not exactly destitute, but it's really..." 
Xu Shangqian felt dizzy. In the end, he could only heave a long sigh.
"Tomorrow I'll go ask if the academy has any copyist work. I'll copy a few more manuscripts..." 
His wife was still complaining by his ear, but Xu Shangqian only felt as if he were falling through clouds, sinking into a deep sleep.

夜聚昼散，鬼市子的灯笼升起又落下好多好多轮。当初莽莽撞撞闯进这里的大侠却好久没回。
小禄想，大侠是不是去江湖了？江湖好玩吗？江湖在哪里呀？
小褔大喊：“那我们就去问问嘛！”
三人跑进鬼市子，问牛头，牛头说，江湖嘛，就是刀啊剑啊的一通乱打。
小禄摇摇头，这真没意思。
她们问银婆婆，银婆婆说，这里就是啊。
小寿摇摇头，这里？鬼市子算是江湖吗？
道主们到茶馆里听说书。鬼先生又在讲与契丹的大战，讲朱帮主，讲鬼市子的阴兵。
道主们点点头，哦，对了，这我们知道的，这真是江湖呢！可是先生，江湖人不是都来来去去找不见的，阴兵怎么一直在这里？
鬼先生道：“大抵是心愿未偿。”
“什么心愿？”
先生道：“或是未曾得见——
#Y【稚儿长成】——稚儿长成，学飞雏鸟不会中途折翼。#E”
en:
As night fell, the lanterns of the Ghostlight Market rose again, as they had through countless turnings of day and night. Yet the wanderer who once recklessly stumbled into this place has not returned for a long, long time.
Lu wondered if the hero had gone off into the jianghu. Was the jianghu a fun place? And where exactly was it?
"Then let's go ask!" Fu cried out.
The three ran into the Ghostlight Market and asked Niu Tou. Niu Tou replied, "The jianghu? It's just a chaotic brawl of clashing sabers and swords."
Lu shook her head. That didn't sound like any fun at all.
Then they asked Granny Yin. Granny Yin said, "Why, this place right here is the jianghu."
Shou shook her head. "Here? Does the Ghostlight Market count as the jianghu?"
The Dao Lords went to the teahouse to listen to storytelling. Mr. Ghost was there again, telling of the great war with the Khitan, of Chief Zhu, and of the spectral soldiers of the Ghostlight Market.
The Dao Lords nodded. "Oh, right, we know that part. This really is the jianghu! But sir, aren't people of the jianghu always coming and going without a trace? Why have the spectral soldiers stayed here all this time?"
Mr. Ghost said, "Most likely, their final wishes remain unfulfilled."
"What wishes?"
Mr. Ghost replied, "Perhaps they never lived to see...
#Y[A child growing up] A child grows to adulthood, and the fledgling learning to fly will not break its wings midway.#E"

zh:
清流既没，四海同悲。五司马者，义贯云霓。虽非同脉而肝胆照，纵存异志唯思言合。兼有支君雨檐，卓荦非常，世之瑰杰。其人也，正当壮年，筋骨若龙虎之健，神采如日月之华。虽处谪迁之困，而意气更凌霄汉。或运筹帷幄，可定乾坤之局；或挥毫泼墨，能醒混沌之世。每见其仗剑长啸，声震林樾，似鹏举九天之志未酬；抚琴高歌，音彻霄壤，若龙吟沧海之思不绝。笔锋未钝，犹能裂帛；文心长赤，岂畏秋霜？
同侪支翁怀远，胸怀济世之志，腹蕴经纶之才，然花甲已逾，鬓发尽凋，形神衰败，恐难胜苦辛。嗟乎！壮年犹可期鹏举，暮齿何堪瘴地劫？
呜呼！孤忠昭昭，可照千古；清流浩浩，足涤八荒。五君魂铸鼎彝，二支名镌星汉。昔阿房宫之烬，鉴秦骄奢；今五司马之谪，岂非天以警世耶？长风浩浩送君去——志若岿岳，岂湮瘴海？心比金石，终耀青史！后人哀之而鉴之，勿使忠魂长羁浊尘矣！
en:
With the virtuous fallen, all beneath heaven mourn. The righteousness of the exiled officials pierces the clouds. Though not of one blood, their loyal hearts shine together; though their paths diverged, they sought accord through honest counsel.
Among them stands Lord Zhi Yuyan, peerless and transcendent, a jewel among men. In the prime of his years, his sinews hold the vigor of dragon and tiger, his spirit the radiance of sun and moon. Though cast into exile, his spirit only rose higher still. At times he could shape the fate of the realm from behind the curtain; at others, his brush could stir a world sunk in darkness. When he raises his sword and roars, the woods tremble, as if his ambition to soar into the Nine Heavens remains unfulfilled. When he plays the zither and sings, his song echoes between earth and sky, like a dragon's endless cry across the sea. His brush has not blunted, capable of tearing through silk; his noble heart burns steadfast, defying the autumn frost.
His companion, Elder Zhi Huaiyuan, holds the ambition to save the realm and the wisdom to govern. Yet past his sixtieth year, his temples frosted and his vitality waning, I fear he cannot endure this bitter hardship. Alas! A man in his prime may still hope to soar, but how can one in his twilight withstand the pestilent wilds?
Alas! Their pure loyalty shines through eternity; the surging righteous current purifies all lands. The souls of these fallen lords are cast in bronze; the names of the two Zhis are engraved among the stars. The ashes of Epang Palace once warned against Qin's extravagance. Does the bitter exile not serve as Heaven's warning to the world?
The great wind carries you onward. With resolve firm as mountains, how could you be swallowed by pestilent seas? With hearts forged like metal and stone, you shall forever shine in the annals of history! Let posterity mourn and take heed, never leaving loyal souls bound to sullied dust!

1. To Qiuniang
Master He is teaching me to write. I did not want to learn. He said learning a few characters would be useful, said then I could write to people. Qiuniang, then I will write to you. I miss you. I keep thinking... it would have been better if I had gone with you...
……
2. To Miao
I dream of you all the time, Miao. You and your mother are both gone. Why am I still here, still alive... I worked the fields all my life. How did I still let your mother and you starve? What kind of farming is that?
……
3. To Miao
Miao, I failed you. I did not keep watch over you... that dirt was not to be eaten, not that much... I know you were hungry. I know you were hungry...
……
4. To Miao
I have learned a few more characters now. If only I could have taught them to you. They even gave me a proper name, Liu Sinong. Heh... I have a real name now. No one calls me Gouzi anymore. They say they are studying farming. Farming... what is there to study?
……
5. To Qiuniang
This place is full of strange people. They call me "Master Farmer." They want me to write a book. We who work the fields were always treated like dogs. Since when could people like us be called "master"? If only you and Miao were still here... Back in the village, the fortune teller used to say people are born again in another life. In your next life, I hope you both be born into a good family, with full bellies every day. And if the place you go is no better... they say one day everyone will have enough to eat... Can that really happen? Can there really be a day when no one goes hungry?

zh: “博古”一词最早见于汉代张衡《西京赋》，而后续多指研究古器物的文人雅集活动。北宋以来，此类雅集大规模展开，时人亦多编纂金石学作品。博古观其器、考制度、正名物，亦能观器省身，以追圣贤之遗风。
en: A term first coined in Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Western Capital in the Han Dynasty. It refers to elegant gatherings of scholars dedicated to studying ancient relics. The practice flourished during the Northern Song Dynasty, sparking a golden age of archaeology focused on ancient bronzes and stone inscriptions. To these scholars, examining an artifact was never just about history. It was a deeply spiritual exercise. By analyzing the craftsmanship of a millennia-old vessel, they sought to connect with the wisdom of the ancient sages and reflect on their own moral character.

zh:
论文摘要：人欲善消暑，必先得其冰。墨山道诸匠，苦夏久矣。经数日研造，方制成随身冰鉴数种，凡行路、摆摊、宿舍躺平，皆可携之。

——正文——

《调语》记载：“冰，水为之，而化于暑。”故保冰之道，首在隔热。前有冰鉴内置夹层，然随身之器，冰少而暑多，片刻即化。

墨山道诸匠苦思数日，作随身冰鉴法：取芦絮叠为七层，使之如剥葫芦，剥了一重，又见一重。内藏冰，外涂蜡，层间留隙，以隔暑气。

又法：人有言，夏日着白衣者，较他者甚凉。乃以白铅粉调胶，通体涂冰鉴。暑日当空，白面反射烈日，则暑气不侵。注：慎勿以舌舐，舐者口烂。

又思：暑气可吸否？乃作三法：湿布虹吸，硝石内胆，木炭吞热。

湿布虹吸，由布裹冰鉴，尾垂水盂。风蒸发则吸热。
硝石内胆，则于夹层置硝石与水，行路摇之，溶则吸热。臂酸可挂腰，晃之自混。
木炭吞热，需烧炭密封罐中，埋入夹层吸暑。每两时辰换之，炭晒干可再用。

此法三则，各有所长：懒人用湿布，勤人摇硝石，会过日子者烧木炭。诸匠试于三伏，冰半日不化，遂录之。
en:
Abstract: He who would ward off the summer heat must first obtain ice. The craftsmen of Mohist Hill had long suffered the summer's toil. After days of research and toil, they at last devised several kinds of portable ice chests, fit to be carried whether on the road, at a market stall, or lying idle in one's dormitory.

- Main Text -

As recorded in "Full of Ai": "Ice is made from water, and melts away in the summer heat." Thus the way of preserving ice lies first in insulating against heat. Earlier ice chests had inner layers built in, yet portable vessels hold little ice against much heat, and melt within moments.

The craftsmen of Mohist Hill pondered for days, and devised a method for a portable ice chest: take reed catkins and layer them sevenfold, so that, like peeling a gourd, one layer reveals another beneath. Ice is stored within, wax applied without, and gaps left between the layers to block out the summer air.

A further method: it is said that those who wear white in summer feel far cooler than others. And so white lead powder was mixed with glue and coated over the entire ice chest. Beneath the blazing summer sun, the white surface reflects the fierce rays, and the heat cannot penetrate within. Note: on no account lick it with the tongue, for those who do shall find their mouths blistered.

A further thought: can the summer air itself be drawn out? And so three methods were devised: damp-cloth siphoning, saltpeter inner chamber, and charcoal heat-absorption.

Damp-cloth siphoning: the ice chest is wrapped in cloth, its end hanging into a water basin. As the wind causes evaporation, heat is drawn away.
Saltpeter inner chamber: saltpeter and water are placed within the inner layer; shaking it as one walks, the saltpeter dissolves and draws away heat. Should the arm tire, it may be hung at the waist, where walking alone will stir it.
Charcoal heat-absorption: burnt charcoal must be sealed within a jar and buried within the inner layer to absorb the heat. It should be changed every two hours, and the charcoal may be dried in the sun and used again.

These three methods each have their own strengths: the idle man uses the damp cloth, the diligent man shakes the saltpeter, and he who truly knows how to live well burns the charcoal. The craftsmen tested these methods through the dog days of summer and found the ice did not melt for half a day, and so they recorded it thus.

en:
Also known as "scooping paper" (Laozhi), sheet forming is the most delicate and demanding step in the craft. Once boiled and beaten, the pulp is poured into a vat. The artisan dips a bamboo screen mould into the slurry and gently sways it back and forth, allowing an even layer of fibers to settle on the screen as the water drains away, forming a wet sheet of paper.
Dipping and rocking the mould requires immense skill: a deeper dip yields thicker paper, while a lighter dip creates a sheer sheet. Achieving perfect consistency relies entirely on muscle memory and keen judgment honed over years of practice.

zh:
天下熙熙皆为利来，天下攘攘皆为利往。而于陈全而言，名利皆为过客。他只图个，畅快一生。

梁乾化二年冬，除夕夜。半零不落的茅草屋内，呼啸的寒风穿过乱石与麦秸的间隙，见证了一个娃娃的呱呱落地。女子伏在床榻上，以柔软的目光注视着这个啼哭的婴孩。未来的日子会如何，谁也不得而知。但她想给孩子最好的祝愿，她希望这孩子能拥有十全十美的人生。她和一边的丈夫相识一笑，给娃娃赐名，叫陈全。

陈全在地里打滚的那几年，正逢乱世，又遭饥荒，日子实在称不上好。但他随他父母，最会苦中作乐。父亲常同他说，人活一世，最长也不过几十载，若时时心存忧虑，实在是白来这一遭。陈全把这话放在了心上。他爱花爱草，爱世间所有的好与不好。即便是父母因病双双亡故的那一年，他也不曾忘记父亲的嘱托。生死亦是人生常态，活下来的人，依旧要好好的活。

后来，陈全带着父母的嘱托，去了很多地方，结识了很多人，寻见了许多喜爱之物。而其中最者，唯酒是也。醉时见天见地，如梦似幻，更添趣味。但他这般心性，不免遭人诟病。有人在他醉时来寻麻烦，反叫他在醉中领悟出了一套别样的功法。再后来……不知怎么的，打啊打的，他就渐渐打响了醉拳客的名号。门派长老欲揽他入门，他大手一挥，笑着拜别。贵人想招他入府，他摇摇晃晃，潇洒离去。江湖人谈起醉拳客，都心有好奇，也不知这世上，还有什么能将他束缚。而醉拳客自己给出了答案。

晋开运四年，契丹攻城，开封大乱。战后，被重挫的鬼市子重建。而醉拳客，成了鬼市子的一员。他能不被名利所缚，却逃不过恩义二字。鬼市子朱佑生曾于危难时救他一命，他于是成了九流门和鬼市子的醉拳客。但他还是原来那副样子，喝着最烈的酒，在各方天地自在盘旋。外人都不信陈全这样的人，真的会为鬼市子和九流门付出性命。陈全也不在意。他出生在最冷的冬夜，却过了最热烈的一生，已然知足。如若真的到了那一天，他会抛下他的酒，去赴那场最畅快的盛宴。
en:
The whole world is bustling with pursuits of profit. But to Chen Quan, fame and fortune were mere passersby. All he ever wanted was to live freely and fulfilled.

In the winter of the second year of Qianhua, Liang dynasty, on New Year's Eve, the wind howled through the gaps in stone and straw of a half-collapsed thatched hut. It bore witness to the cry of a newborn child. A woman lay on the bed as she softly gazed at the baby in her arms. No one could know what fate awaited this child, but she wished him the very best—a life lived fully and completely. She and her husband shared a quiet smile as they named their son Chen Quan.

Chen Quan grew up rolling through the fields during years of war and famine. Life was far from good, but he and his parents knew how to find joy in times of hardship. His father often said that a person lives no more than a few decades, so what's the point of always worrying? Might as well enjoy the ride. Chen Quan took those words to heart. He loved flowers and weeds, the beautiful and the broken. Even in the year both his parents died of illness, he didn't forget his father's teachings. Life and death are part of the same road; those who live must live well.

So Chen Quan set out with their words in mind. He traveled far, met many people, and found many things to love. And among them all, what he loved the most was wine. When drunk, he could see heaven and earth, and float between dream and reality. It was so much fun. Of course, a man like that would draw mockery. Someone once picked a fight with him while he was drunk—only to find Chen Quan, in his haze, inventing a whole new style of combat. And so, without meaning to, he became known as the Drunk Martial Artist. Sect elders tried to recruit him, but he waved and laughed as he walked away. Nobles offered him patronage, and he staggered off with a grin. The jianghu spoke of him with wonder, "What could possibly bind a man like that?" Chen Quan himself gave them the answer.

In the fourth year of Kaiyun, Jin dynasty, the Khitan laid siege to Kaifeng. After the war, the devastated Ghostlight Market was rebuilt, and the Drunk Martial Artist became a member of it. He had no use for fame or wealth. But gratitude—that was different. It was Zhu Yousheng of the Ghostlight Market who had once saved his life. So Chen Quan joined both the Nine Mortal Ways and the Ghostlight Market. Still the same as ever, he drank the strongest wine and danced freely across heaven and earth. Outsiders doubted that someone like him would ever give his life for anyone. But he didn't care. He was born on the coldest winter night, yet lived the warmest, most blazing life. That was enough. And if the day ever came, he would put down his wine, and step into the grandest feast of all.

zh:
吱——呀——
饸饹面的摊子上水滚声、吆喝声、交谈声错乱嘈杂，小乐天总能从中捕捉到饸饹床子咬合时候的吱呀声。
吱——呀——
又一碗面被轧出来，娘左手伸到饸饹床子下面一抹，右手把汤勺里的臊子浇上去，一碗饸饹面就出炉了。
小乐天总是怀疑，每个人轧饸饹面的声音是不一样的。
爹爹轧饸饹床子的声音轻快，像木头的呼吸声一样。
有次爹爹带他爬山，微风吹过了松林。爹爹教小乐天把耳朵贴到了松树枝干上，他听到的就是爹爹轧面的声音。
爹爹走了以后，小乐天从没见娘亲哭过。
他看着原本不太爱说话的娘，慢慢学着招揽客人，大声地朝客人介绍自己熬的臊子有多新鲜，这面有多筋道。
然后利索地抄起一只碗，放到了饸饹架子下面。
吱——呀——
小乐天听得出来，那是木头在哭的声音。
en:
Squeak... Creak...
Amidst the roar of boiling water and the marketplace din, Little Letian could always pick out that one sound: the groan of the wooden He'le press clamping down.
Squeak... Creak...
Another bowl of noodles slid free. His mother swept her left hand beneath the press, steady and practiced, while her right tipped a ladle of sauce over the noodles. A fresh bowl was ready.
Little Letian was convinced that everyone pressed he'le noodles differently.
His father's pressing had sounded light and lively, like wood breathing.
Once, his father took him into the mountains. A breeze passed through the pine forest, and his father told him to press his ear against the trunk. The sound he heard was exactly the same as when father made noodles, soft, hollow, alive.
After his father passed away, Little Letian never once saw his mother cry.
He watched his mother, who used to be very quiet, learn to call out to customers, raising her voice to praise how fresh her sauce was, and how springy the noodles were.
Then she would reach for a bowl, swift and sure, and slide it beneath the press.
Squeak... Creak...
Little Letian knew that sound now. It wasn't wood breathing anymore, but wood crying.

Qin Yang, a swordsman skilled in theft, crafty by nature, mediocre in martial arts, and notoriously vicious in character.

Summary:
On an unspecified date, Qin Yang got drunk at a tavern in town and quarreled with others. In his drunken boasting, he claimed that no one under heaven could match him, and even said he had taken part in the famous showdown at Mount Mang between masters of the Turkic lands and the Central Plains. The absurd claim drew ridicule.
Qin Yang then declared that the two masters who had contended for the title of "Greatest Under Heaven" had in fact died by his treachery. After saying so, he went so far as to stomp on another man's face, humiliating him beyond endurance. The crowd flew into a rage and beat Qin Yang to death on the spot.

Result:
Qin Yang died at the scene. The killers were local hoodlums and were later imprisoned.

Note:
This case is closed. Preserved as an old record and approved for consultation.

zh:
醉仙月的客房永远热热闹闹。小二为往来客人斟上离人泪，听五湖四海的侠客操着不同的口音讲着各地的见闻。但当他们饮尽杯中酒时，所有的语言都变成满足的喟叹。你突然想到，上次刀哥来不羡仙后，还没有坐在这里，喝上一壶你亲自斟满的酒。
有那样一把好刀的人，唯有世间的好酒才可相配。若是要去见刀哥，你定要准备一壶……
⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛
你提着酒壶来到刀哥坟前，替他去了碑上的落叶。你记得在瓷窑初见时他的嘲讽，也记得在破庙中他的坦诚。你们说好一起要去江湖，去看看外面的世界。可他却像闯入你生活里的一场风暴，轰轰烈烈为你揭开了江湖的一角，然后便消散世间。是的，消散，如日光下的雪，似流水中的盐，无从搜寻。唯有一身怅然，尽付壶中酒。
en:
The Drunken Immortal Month is always bustling with life. The waiter pours Parting Tears for wanderers from all corners of the world, who are trading stories of their travels in varying accents. When they drain their cups, all words soften into contented sighs. You think of Blade's last visit and the cup you never poured for him.
A man with such a fine blade deserves only the finest wine in the world. If you are going to see Blade, you must prepare a pot of...

You bring a wine pot to Blade's grave and brush the fallen leaves from his tombstone. You remember his sneer when you first met at the porcelain kiln, and his blunt honesty in the ruined temple. You had agreed to venture into the jianghu together, to see the world outside. Yet he burst into your life like a fierce storm, dramatically tearing back a corner of the jianghu for you, only to vanish from this earth. Yes, he vanished, like snow under sunlight or salt in flowing water, nowhere to be found, leaving you with nothing but a deep sorrow, all poured into the wine in your pot.

zh:
创建房间：
玩家可自由创建砺兵台房间，创房成功后会自动成为房主，拥有该房间内成员管理权与出战安排权限。房主可以向房间内其他成员转让房主身份，若房主直接退出则会自动把房主权限转让给房间内人气值最高的成员。

赛制：
房主可设置该房间的挑战模式，分为自由模式和管理模式。
自由模式下，房间内玩家可自由选择场内成员或队伍发起叫阵或指名挑战；
管理模式下，房间内玩家或队长报名后，由房主决定对战双方；
胜负判定分为三种：一局一胜、三局两胜和五局三胜；
砺兵台目前支持1V1和2V2、3V3、5V5队伍对战；另外还支持觉障林1V1、2V2和5V5队伍作战；以及群策3V3、4V4和5V5对战模式。

人气值及房间热度：
在房间内收到赠礼会增加个人的人气值。房间内人数越多、战斗次数和赠礼次数越多，房间的热度值越高。每日凌晨5点会重新计算各房间的热度及房间内各成员的人气值。
en:
Create Room:
Players can freely create Training Terrace rooms. Upon successful creation, they automatically become the host, with member management and battle arrangement permissions. The host can transfer host status to other members in the room. If the host exits directly, host permissions are automatically transferred to the member with the highest Popularity in the room.

Format:
The host can set the room's Challenge mode to Free Mode or Management Mode.
In Free Mode, players in the room can freely choose members or teams to issue a challenge or designate a challenge.
In Management Mode, after players or team leaders sign up, the host decides the opposing sides.
Victory determination is divided into three types: one win, best-of-three, and best-of-five.
Training Terrace currently supports 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, and 5v5 team battles; it also supports Perception Forest 1v1, 2v2, and 5v5 team battles.

Popularity and Room Heat:
Receiving gifts in the room increases personal Popularity. The more people in the room, the more battles and gifts, the higher the room's Heat value. Every day at 05:00 AM, the Heat of each room and the Popularity of each member in the room are recalculated.

这几日奶奶记起你了，想和你约酒，我不允，改寄松子和橡子一包。都是跟着飞鼠挑的，个大饱满。

另外还有一份，请大侠帮忙带给阿沱先生，他一人住在墨城外的山坡上。信鸪常在那边迷路，故请大侠帮忙。天气转凉，阿沱先生许久未来卧星岩。奶奶虽然偶尔才能记起他，但打心底颇为挂念。多谢大侠帮我走一趟，得空来卧星岩坐坐，月鹿请你吃饭！

对了，再帮我问问阿沱先生，他上回答应讲的“无名客”的故事，何时讲给我听呀？
en:
$N,

Long time no see. How have you been lately?
Grandma remembered you these past few days and wanted to share a drink with you. I wouldn't allow it, so I'm sending along a packet of pine nuts and acorns instead. Flying Squirrel helped pick them out. They're all big and full.

There's one more letter as well. Please help deliver it to Tuo, who lives on the hillside outside Mohist City. My messenger dove often loses its way over there, so I must trouble you to help. The weather is turning cold, and Tuo has not come to Stellabed Rocks for quite some time. Grandma may only remember him now and then, but she truly misses him deep down. Thank you for making the trip on my behalf. If you have the time, do come by Stellabed Rocks sometime, and I'll treat you to a meal.

Oh, and please ask Tuo one more thing for me. Last time, he promised to tell me the story of the "Nameless Wanderer." When will he finally tell it to me?
Shu Rong
