【僖公第五】

元年，春，王正月。
公何以不言即位？继弑君，子不言即位。此非子也，其称子何？臣子一例也。
〇齐师、宋师、曹师次于聂北救邢。
救不言次，此其言次何？不及事也。不及事者何？邢已亡矣。孰亡之？盖狄灭之。曷为不言狄灭之？为桓公讳也。曷为为桓公讳？上无天子，下无方伯，天下诸侯有相灭亡者，桓公不能救，则桓公耻之。曷为先言次而后言救？君也。君则其称师何？不与诸侯专封也。曷为不与？实与而文不与。文曷为不与？诸侯之义，不得专封也。诸侯之义不得专封，则其曰实与之何？上无天子，下无方伯，天下诸侯有相灭亡者，力能救之，则救之可也。
〇夏，六月，邢迁于陈仪。
迁者何？其意也。迁之者何？非其意也。
〇齐师、宋师、曹师城邢。
此一事也，曷为复言"齐师、宋师、曹师不复言师，则无以知其为一事也。"
〇秋，七月，戊辰，夫人姜氏薨于夷，齐人以归。
夷者何？齐地也。齐地则其言齐人以归何？夫人薨于夷，则齐人以归。夫人薨于夷，则齐人曷为以归？桓公召而缢杀之。楚人伐郑。八月，公会齐侯、宋公、郑伯、曹伯、邾娄人于朾。

……
en:
[Chapter 5: Lord Xi]

It was the duke's first year, the spring, the king's first month.
Why does the Annals not state that the Lord "ascended the throne"? When succeeding a lord who was assassinated, a son does not state that he ascended the throne. He was not the son, so why is he treated here as a son? The principle for a minister and a son is one and the same in this context.
The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao halted at Niebei to rescue Xing.
An action of rescue does not normally mention a "halt." Why does it mention a "halt" here? Because they were too late for the event. What does "too late for the event" mean? Xing had already perished. Who destroyed it? It was probably the Di barbarians who destroyed it. Why does the Annals not explicitly state that the Di destroyed it? It is to conceal the failure on behalf of Lord Huan. Why conceal it for Lord Huan? Above there was no powerful Son of Heaven, and below there was no leader among the feudal lords. When the lords of the world destroyed one another, and Lord Huan failed to rescue them, Lord Huan considered it a disgrace. Why is the "halt" mentioned before the "rescue"? Because the rulers personally led the armies. If the rulers led them, why does the text only refer to them as "armies"? It is because the Annals does not grant feudal lords the right to arbitrarily enfeoff or re-establish states. Why not grant it? In reality, Lord Huan granted it, but the text does not grant it. Why does the wording not grant it? According to the righteousness of feudal lords, they are not permitted to arbitrarily enfeoff states. If their righteousness does not permit arbitrary enfeoffment, then why is it said that he "in reality granted it"? Above there was no Son of Heaven, and below there was no leader among the lords. If a state among the lords of the world was about to perish, and one had the power to rescue it, then rescuing it was permissible.
In summer, the sixth month, Xing was relocated to Chenyi.
What is meant by "relocate"? It means it was done by their own will. What is meant by "relocated"? It means it was against their own will.
The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao built walls for Xing.
This and the previous entry belong to the same continuous undertaking. Why are "the armies of Qi, Song, and Cao" mentioned again? If "the armies" were not repeated, there would be no way for the reader to know that this was part of the exact same continuous achievement.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the wuchen day, the Lord's wife, Lady Jiang, passed away in Yi, and the people of Qi took her remains back.
What was Yi? It was Qi territory. Since it was Qi territory, why does the text say "the people of Qi took her back"? Because the Lady passed away in Yi, the people of Qi consequently took her back. The Lady passed away on Qi territory, but why did the people of Qi take her back? Lord Huan summoned her there and had her strangled to death. The people of Chu attacked Zheng. In the eighth month, the Lord met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a person of Zhulou at Ting.

雾隐谷中，残局之前，师徒对坐。
七日推演，星盘棋间，皆是死局。代表“封龙书院”的白子，已被围困得只剩最后一息。
“师父......”弟子垂首，声涩如沙，“封龙书院，已是死棋。去再多人，不过是为这盘败局，再添一枚无用的弃子。”
谢韫不语，只捻起一颗白子，决然叩向天元。清响落定，满盘皆寂。
望着弟子不解的目光，谢韫缓缓开口：“局虽死，焉知此局非一子？”
她站起身，望向谷外的重重白雾。“局，早已不在滹沱。”
她没有再说下去，只将那枚阵亡的白子从棋盘上拾起，轻轻放回了弟子手中。
“只是这局，还需要一子。”
en:
Master and disciple sat before a lost game in Mist-Hidden Vale.
Seven days of deduction on the star-map board yielded only a dead end. The white stones, representing Dragonbend Academy, were cornered to their last breath.
"Master," the disciple whispered, voice dry as sand, "Dragonbend Academy is a dead game. No matter how many we send, they will only be futile sacrifices."
Xie Yun remained silent. She lifted a white stone and struck it firmly onto the center of the board. The sharp click echoed in the silence.
Meeting her disciple's bewildered gaze, Xie Yun said slowly, "The game may be dead, but who is to say this entire board is not just a single stone?"
She stood, looking at the heavy white mist outside the vale. "The true game is no longer at the Hutuo."
She said no more. She merely picked up the sacrificed white stone from the board and placed it gently back into the disciple's hand.
"But for that game, we still need one more stone."

zh:
奔走半生，她终于赶至命运的终点。
此地幽寂，如当年那方漂流黑匣，光影昏暝。
她闭上眼睛，似乎这一生都得以重头来过了。她仍是少时模样，师父令她在静室运炁。她闭着眼，耳朵却伸出老长，满树蝉嘶如沸，万师师兄又在骂师父了，而那个人……书页轻翻，如夏风拂叶。他究竟在看什么呢，一本薄册不过几十页，偏被他读得千回百转。那书中值得留恋的，究竟是什么呀？
她暗催内炁，魂灵游走出窍，恍惚已至他身畔，多想窥一眼那书间字句，额上却忽地一痛——“喂，运炁要静心呀。”
奇怪，师父怎知她的心猿意马？
这一槌，把她伸出的手掀了回去，把她游走的炁锤回现在。
是啊，原来已经过去这么久了。昔日雀跃心，早沉作深潭静水。此地再无道争之喧，空余机簧咬合的铮鸣。
如今她炁盛可启天衍，却再回不到那个蝉声满树的午后。
天衍阵枢接入经脉，传来噬骨之痛，此刻，她多想再记起那一味香气。

那是初入墨山道的某年冬夜，因路见不平，她再度误了归家时辰，最终只得浑身湿冷迟迟夜归。
可推开家门，竟闻到一股渍花蜜糕般的香甜气息——这烛芯不知捻了何料，竟有她最贪的甜食滋味。
灶上还煨着粥，万师师兄正专注地修着木鸢，师父已睡得香甜，那人不过顺手往她常坐的席边放下一只软垫。
无人特意唤她，可在那暖烘烘的甜香之中，她忽然明白了何以为家。
这般温暖，她也曾想永驻其中。

无奈烽烟又起，流民泣途。
她在阵前杀伐间，望见本该升起炊烟的村落，此刻空余焚火。她顿悟墨门所求的桃源，不过是让千万如她之人，皆有一缕炊烟可盼，有家可归。
于是她转身赴风雨，向山外行去。又投身算阵之事，以期终有一日可洞晓天地万机，世间得恒久长宁。
此去经年，因事失约无数，再难闻见那般甜暖烛香。
偶尔赶路途径山野人家，看见窗内透出的微弱火光，她总忍不住驻足片刻，想象着里面是否也有一个如她当年那般困倦归家的人，此刻正被暖意轻轻接住。
待天下事了，自己也归家罢。

心跳渐与机簧同律，那缕等候的香气再难忆起。
师父说，运炁要静心。她想她学会了。
可万念俱寂时，一声鸟鸣而已，她又记起那些旧事，那味暖烘烘的香气。
……咦，他怎么在这？

或许是她仍信着，只要一直走，往前，往上，总有一日能摘得天上月。
那时他必穿过人群，一眼认出她来。
然后假装不知眼前是失约的惯犯、夺命的凶手，只微笑着说——
“回来了。”
渍花蜜糕的香气中，她终于读到了他读的那一页。
en:
After walking half a lifetime, she has finally arrived at journey's end.
This place is still and silent, much like that drifting black chest from long ago, wrapped in the half-light of dusk.

She closes her eyes, and it is as though her whole life might begin again from the very start.
She is young once more, told by her Master to circulate her Qi in the quiet chamber.
Eyes shut, her ears stretch out as far as they can reach. The trees are alive with cicada song. Senior Brother Zhang Wanshi is scolding Master again. And that man... the soft rustle of turning pages drifts through the room like a summer breeze through leaves.
What could he possibly be reading? A slim little booklet, only a few dozen pages, yet he returns to it again and again as though it holds something inexhaustible. What is it that keeps him there?

Unable to help herself, she quietly stirs her inner Qi. Her spirit slips free and drifts to his side, straining for a glimpse of the words on the page, when a sharp rap lands squarely on her forehead.
"Still your mind if you want to guide your Qi."
Strange. How had Master known her thoughts were wandering?

That one knock drives back her reaching hand and pulls her stray Qi back into the present.

Indeed... so much time has passed. The restlessness of her younger years has long since settled into the still depths of a quiet pool. The clamor of clashing ideals is gone, leaving only the cold, steady turning of interlocking gears. Her Qi has grown vast enough to awaken the Deriviation formation, yet she can never return to that summer afternoon alive with the sound of cicadas.
As the formation pivot anchors to her meridians, bringing an agony that gnaws through to the bone, she finds herself wishing above all else to remember one particular fragrance.

It was a winter night in her early years at Mohist Hill. She had stopped to right an injustice on her way home and arrived late again, soaked to the skin and shivering with cold. But the moment she pushed open the door, a sweetness like honeyed flower cakes washed over her. Whatever had been worked into the candlewick carried the scent of the sweets she loved most.
Porridge simmered on the stove. Senior Brother Zhang Wanshi sat absorbed in repairing a wooden eagle. Master had already drifted off to sleep. And that man had simply, quietly set a soft cushion beside her usual seat.

No one called her name. Yet within that warm, honeyed fragrance, she suddenly understood what it meant to have a home. Such warmth. Once, she had wished to stay inside it forever.

But the fires of war rose again, and refugees crowded the roads in tears. Amid the fighting at the front, she looked toward villages where cooking smoke should have curled into the sky and found only smoldering ruins. It came to her then: the Haven the Mohists sought was simply a world where thousands like her could each have a thread of hearth smoke to look toward, and a home to return to.

And so she turned to face the storm and walked out beyond the mountains. She threw herself into the study of formations, hoping that one day she might read the workings of the world entire and bring lasting peace to the realm.

The years passed. Leaving behind her a trail of broken promises, she rarely caught that sweet warm scent of candle smoke again. Now and then, passing a lone cottage in the wilds and seeing a faint glow through the window, she could not help but stop for a moment. She wondered whether someone in there was also coming home worn and weary, and being gently held by the warmth waiting inside.
When the world's troubles are at an end, I too shall go home.

Slowly, her heartbeat fell into rhythm with the turning gears, and the fragrance that had once waited for her grew harder to recall. Master had said, "Still your mind to guide your Qi." She thought she had finally learned how.
Yet when every last thought went quiet, a single birdcall was enough to bring it all flooding back: the old memories, and that warm, sweet smell.

...Wait. Why is he here?

Perhaps she had never stopped believing that if she kept walking, forward and upward, she would one day reach up and take the moon from the sky. When that day came, he would surely make his way through the crowd and find her at a single glance. Then, pretending not to notice that the woman before him was a habitual breaker of promises and a bringer of death, he would simply smile and say,

"You're back."

Amid the scent of honeyed flower cakes, she finally read the page he had lingered on for so long.

zh:
赵晓刚十四岁那年，他爹问他，想不想学做饭。
不是淘米下锅那种做饭。是靠这个吃饭。
他爹在镇上馆子里掌了二十年勺，左边肩膀比右边高出一截——常年歪着脖子看火候看的。赵晓刚蹲在院子里，攥着根狗尾巴草想了半天，说，学。
头三天，他爹没让他上灶。叫他蹲在后门口择葱。黄叶掐掉，老皮剥掉，根须剪掉。他蹲了一上午，腿麻了，站起来眼前发黑。他爹从他择好的那一小把里又挑出一半不合格的，说，葱不干净，菜就好不了。你爹这二十年，头三年全在择葱。
第十天，他爹叫他尝葱。三捆葱各抽一根，掰断了生嚼。第一根辣得冲鼻子，第二根发甜，第三根有土腥味。他爹说，沙土地里长的水少，甜味攒住了。洼地里水多，辣味浮在面上。你得尝。尝不出来，就不知道料的本性。不知道料的本性，使唤不动它。
一个月后，开始剁肉馅。肥瘦三七开，剁成石榴籽大小。他剁了一上午，胳膊酸得抬不起来。他爹抓一把他剁的馅，手松开，肉粘成一坨。又抓一把自己剁的，松开，肉粒散在案板上。
“刀是往下剁，不是往下砸。剁是切断筋，砸是把肉砸烂了。筋断了，下锅才嫩。肉烂了，下锅就柴。”
他重新拿起刀。一下一下，刀刃触到肉的瞬间往回收一点力。
收工时他爹把他新剁的馅团成丸子下锅煮了，切开，一人一半。他咬了一口，弹牙。
那天晚上他爹头一回让他站灶边看炒菜。火光映在脸上，他爹左边肩膀高出一截，脖子歪着，眼睛却亮得很。
“晓刚，做菜这东西，说到底就一句话。人哄料，料哄人。最后哄的是嘴，是心。”
赵晓刚把这句话咽进肚子里。和那三根生葱、那把石榴籽大小的肉馅一起，咽了十年。
他爹走的那年冬天，已经吃不下东西了。最后那天下午忽然说要吃丸子。他赶紧剁馅调葱下油锅，端到床边。他爹咬了一口又一口，竟吃了大半个。
第二天早上他爹走了。
赵晓刚在灶房里蹲了一上午，把剩下的肉馅全炸了，端到村口分给过路的人。人家咬一口，说香。
第二年开春，他回村支了自己的摊。
从镇上铁匠铺敲了十七口锅，挑出那口厚墩墩的。支摊头一天，他站在村口老井边，把嗓子眼里憋了十年的那声吆喝喊了出来。
“大葱——选硬挺咧——”
拿铁勺往锅沿上一敲。
“铛——”
厚实铛铛的一声。从锅心荡到锅沿，像往老井里丢了颗石子儿，回声绵长。
en:
When Zhao Xiaogang was fourteen, his father asked him if he wanted to learn to cook.
He didn't mean boiling rice for the family dinner. He meant cooking to put a roof over their heads.
His dad had worked the woks at a restaurant in town for twenty years. His left shoulder sat permanently higher than his right, a stiff, twisted posture earned from decades of tilting his neck to watch the flames. Squatting in the dirt courtyard, Xiaogang rolled a blade of foxtail grass between his fingers for a long time before finally nodding. "I'll learn."
For the first three days, his dad didn't let him within ten feet of a stove. Instead, he made the boy squat by the back door and prep leeks. Pinch off the yellowed leaves, peel the tough outer skins, and snip the roots. Xiaogang squatted there all morning until his legs went dead. When he finally stood, black spots danced in his vision. His dad picked through the meager pile, tossed half of it in the trash, and shook his head. "If the leeks aren't clean, the dish is already dead. For my first three years, I didn't touch anything but leeks."
On the tenth day, his dad made him taste them. He pulled a stalk from three different bundles, snapped them in half, and handed them over to be chewed raw. The first burned his nose, the second carried a subtle sweetness, and the third tasted like straight mud. "Sandy soil doesn't hold water, so the sweetness concentrates," his dad explained. "Wetlands hold too much, so the harsh spice floats right to the top. You have to taste it. If you don't know the true nature of what you're cooking, you can't command it."
A month later, he was handed a cleaver and told to mince pork. Thirty percent fat, seventy percent lean, chopped down to the exact size of pomegranate seeds. Xiaogang chopped all morning until his arm was dead weight. His dad scooped up a handful of Xiaogang's meat and dropped it. It hit the board in a dense, sticky lump. Then, he grabbed a handful of his own. When he dropped it, the tiny morsels of meat scattered cleanly across the wood.
"The blade chops. It doesn't smash," his dad corrected. "Chopping severs the sinew. Smashing just turns it to mush. Break the sinew, and it fries up tender. Mash it, and it cooks up like old leather."
Xiaogang picked up the cleaver again. Strike by strike, he learned to pull his punch, just a fraction, the very second the steel met the meat.
When the prep was done, his dad rolled the newly minced meat into a ball, boiled it, sliced it in two, and gave Xiaogang half. Xiaogang took a bite. It had a perfect, springy snap.
That night, for the first time, his dad let him stand by the wok and watch him fry. The firelight flickered across the old man's face. His left shoulder was hunched, his neck twisted, but his eyes were blazing.
"Xiaogang, cooking boils down to one simple truth. You serve the ingredients well, and they'll serve you. But at the end of the day, what you're really trying to comfort is the mouth, and the heart."
Zhao Xiaogang swallowed those words. Along with the bite of raw leeks and the rhythm of the cleaver, he locked them away inside for ten long years.
The winter his dad died, the old man had completely stopped eating. But on his final afternoon, out of nowhere, he asked for a meatball. Xiaogang scrambled. He minced the pork, prepped the leeks, fired up the wok, and rushed a steaming bowl to the bedside. His dad took a bite, and then another, miraculously managing to finish more than half.
The next morning, he was gone.
Xiaogang sat alone in the kitchen for hours. Eventually, he fired up the oil, fried the rest of the minced meat into meatballs, carried the basket out to the edge of the village, and handed them out to passing travelers. People took one bite and praised his cooking.
When spring rolled around the following year, he moved back home and set up his own stall.
He tested seventeen woks at the town smithy's before finding that heavy, thick-bottomed iron. And on his first day of business, standing by the old stone well at the edge of town, he finally let out the shout he'd been holding in his chest for a decade.
"Leeks gotta be crisp and firm!"
He took his iron ladle and cracked it against the rim of the wok.
CLANG!
A thick, heavy, resonant chime. It rippled from the center of the iron to the rim, echoing long and deep, like a stone dropped down an ancient well.

zh:
【桓公第二】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。
继弑君不言即位，此其言即位何？如其意也。
〇三月，公会郑伯于垂。
〇郑伯以璧假许田。
其言以璧假之何？易之也。易之则其言假之何？为恭也。曷为为恭？有天子存，则诸侯不得专地也。许田者何？鲁朝宿之邑也。诸侯时朝乎天子，天子之郊，诸侯皆有朝宿之邑焉。此鲁朝宿之邑也，则曷为谓之许田？讳取周田也。讳取周田，则曷为谓之许田？系之许也。曷为系之许？近许也。此邑也，其称田何？田多邑少称田，邑多田少称邑。
〇夏，四月，丁未，公及郑伯盟于越。
〇秋，大水。
何以书？记灾也。
〇冬，十月。

二年，春，王正月，戊申，宋督弑其君与夷及其大夫孔父。
及者何？累也。弑君多矣，舍此无累者乎？曰：有，仇牧、荀息皆累也。舍仇牧、荀息无累者乎？曰：有。有则此何以书？贤也。何贤乎孔父？孔父可谓义形于色矣。其义形于色奈何？督将弑殇公，孔父生而存，则殇公不可得而弑也，故于是先攻孔父之家。殇公知孔父死，己必死，趋而救之，皆死焉。孔父正色而立于朝，则人莫敢过而致难于其君者，孔父可谓义形于色矣。
〇滕子来朝。
〇三月，公会齐侯、陈侯、郑伯于稷，以成宋乱。
内大恶讳，此其目言之何？远也。所见异辞，所闻异辞，所传闻异辞。隐亦远矣，曷为为隐讳？隐贤而桓贱也。
〇夏，四月，取郜大鼎于宋。
此取之宋，其谓之郜鼎何？器从名，地从主人。器何以从名？地何以从主人？器之与人，非有即尔。宋始以不义取之，故谓之郜鼎。至乎地之与人则不然，俄而可以为其有矣。然则为取，可以为其有乎？曰：否。何者？若楚王之妻媦，无时焉可也。戊申，纳于大庙。何以书？讥。何讥尔？遂乱受赂，纳于大庙，非礼也。
〇秋，七月，纪侯来朝。
〇蔡侯、郑伯会于邓。
离不言会，此其言会何？盖邓与会尔。
〇九月，入耜。
〇公及戎盟于唐。
〇冬，公至自唐。

……
en:
【Duke Huan, Year 2】

First year, spring, the king's first month, the duke assumed the throne.
When a ruler is assassinated, the succession is not announced. Why is it announced here? Because it was according to his wishes.
〇In the third month, the duke met with the Earl of Zheng at Chui.
〇The Earl of Zheng exchanged the jade bi for the fields of Xu.
Why does it say "exchanged with a jade bi"? Because it was a trade. If it was a trade, why say "exchanged"? To show respect. Why show respect? Because while the Emperor exists, the feudal lords cannot arbitrarily control land. What were the fields of Xu? They were the lodging town of Lu for court visits. The feudal lords paid regular court visits to the Emperor, and in the suburbs of the Emperor, each feudal lord had a lodging town. Since this was the lodging town of Lu, why call it the fields of Xu? To avoid mentioning the seizure of Zhou land. If avoiding the seizure of Zhou land, why call it the fields of Xu? Because it was attached to Xu. Why attach it to Xu? Because it was near Xu. This was a town, so why call it fields? When there are more fields than towns, it is called fields; when there are more towns than fields, it is called a town.
〇Summer, fourth month, on the day Dingwei, the duke and the Earl of Zheng formed an alliance at Yue.
〇Autumn, a great flood.
Why is this recorded? To record a disaster.
〇Winter, tenth month.

Second year, spring, the king's first month, on the day Wushen, Song Du assassinated his ruler, Yiyi, and his Grand Doctor Kong Fu.
What does "and" mean here? It means being implicated. There have been many assassinations of rulers; were there none besides this where others were implicated? It is said: Yes, Qiu Mu and Xun Xi were both implicated. Were there none besides Qiu Mu and Xun Xi? It is said: Yes, there were. If there were, why is this one recorded? Because of virtue. What virtue did Kong Fu have? Kong Fu could be said to have righteousness shown on his face. What does it mean that righteousness was shown on his face? Du was about to assassinate Duke Shang, and as long as Kong Fu was alive, Duke Shang could not be assassinated. Therefore, he first attacked Kong Fu's household. Duke Shang knew that once Kong Fu died, he himself would surely die, so he rushed to save him, and both died. Kong Fu stood in the court with a solemn expression, and no one dared to approach and bring harm to his ruler. Kong Fu could be said to have righteousness shown on his face.
〇The Viscount of Teng came to pay a court visit.
〇In the third month, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng at Ji to settle the unrest in Song.
Major internal wrongdoings are concealed. Why are they stated here in detail? Because it was in the distant past. What was seen is described differently, what was heard is described differently, and what was heard by hearsay is described differently. Yin was also distant, so why conceal for Yin? Because Yin was virtuous while Huan was base.
〇Summer, fourth month, the great tripod of Gao was taken from Song.
It was taken from Song, so why call it the Gao tripod? Vessels follow their names, and lands follow their masters. Why do vessels follow their names? Why do lands follow their masters? Vessels and people are not inherently connected. Song first took it unrighteously, so it is called the Gao tripod. As for land and people, it is different; in a short time, it can become one's own. If so, then for taking, can it become one's own? It is said: No. Why? Like the King of Chu marrying his sister, there is never a time when it is acceptable. On the day Wushen, it was placed in the Grand Temple. Why is this recorded? To criticize. What is criticized? Taking bribes after settling chaos and placing them in the Grand Temple is against ritual.
〇Autumn, seventh month, the Marquis of Ji came to pay a court visit.
〇The Marquis of Cai and the Earl of Zheng met at Deng.
When only two parties meet, it is not called a meeting. Why is it called a meeting here? Because Deng participated in the meeting.
〇In the ninth month, entered Si.
〇The duke and the Rong formed an alliance at Tang.
〇Winter, the duke returned from Tang.

……

zh:
归望野小屋外，几位文津馆弟子正在讨论几座石狮子的来历。有人觉得那里是帝王陵墓的神道，有人说那不过是匠人炫技的雕饰，也有人相信那之下藏着失传的秘宝。见你到来，几位弟子纷纷围过来，七嘴八舌地说着自己的看法，并问你怎么看。……
#Y【是故人留笔。】你想起在这里拾到过一支笔。那是画睛兄之物。他画了一幅画，画了一场梦，这石狮子便是闯入他画中的景色。#E
听闻你所言，几位弟子面面相觑。他们挠挠头，半晌才开口说道，此处过去不过是一片荒野，如今赫然出现石狮子，或许是地气地脉异动；另一位则坚持认为此地有帝陵，那狮子便是引路标……见无人与你接话，你也只得暗自苦笑。你回头看了看那只最大石狮子，它依然安静地昂首迎风而立，岿然不动，千古如一。
en:
Outside the little hut at Homeward Wilds, several Inkbound Order disciples are in the middle of a lively debate over the origins of the stone lions. One is certain they once stood along the spirit way of an imperial tomb; another insists they are merely an artisan's flourish, nothing more than a display of skill; a third is convinced that some long-lost treasure must lie hidden beneath them. The moment they spot you, they crowd around at once, chattering over one another to offer their theories and ask what you think...
#Y[A brushstroke left by an old friend.] You remember the brush you once found here. It belonged to Huajing. He painted a picture; he painted a dream. And these stone lions were part of the landscape that wandered into his painting.#E
At your answer, the disciples fall briefly silent and trade bewildered glances. They scratch their heads, and after a long pause, someone ventures that this place used to be nothing but wilderness, so perhaps the sudden appearance of the stone lions is due to some strange stirring in the earth's veins; another still refuses to yield, insisting there must be an imperial tomb here, with the lions marking the way... With no one quite able to follow your meaning, you can only let out a wry, inward smile. Turning back, you look once more at the largest stone lion. en: Good dwelt within the temple, keeping company with the old monk. Whenever the wooden fish sounded, Good would lie curled upon the prayer cushion, nodding along with each knock of the beat. Seeing this, the old monk would always murmur, "Good, good," and so the little cat came by its name. The young novices often wondered, could it be that even so small a creature understood the Buddhist teachings? The old monk would answer thus: "Heaven and earth are vast, and all things within them possess a spirit of their own. Though the cat cannot speak, having gazed upon heaven and earth, it has come to know something of its subtle mysteries." Good understood none of this, and at times found these people rather strange. Why should they spend half a day puzzling over joys that a cat could find simply by dozing in the sun and kneading its paws? Good would never know what thoughts passed through the old monk's mind, nor would the old monk ever know what stirred in Good's heart. Only the morning bell and evening drum kept company with these two quiet shadows, as they passed one year after another.

zh:
一日夜晚，卖肉夹馍的师傅正要收摊回家。他摇了摇碗里剩下的肉，愁眉苦脸地叹了口气。
这荒郊野外的，就算这馍馍香出十里地，也没人愿意吃哇！
喵……喵喵！巴掌大的小猫闻了味道，听了声音，怯生生地挨到师傅的脚边。
一个猫能吃多少？师傅这么想着，丢下一块肉去。
从此往后，在这荒郊野外，肉夹馍摊每天必有一位喵喵叫的客人。
不知为何，村里突然多了许多江湖人。小猫天天蹲在摊旁，来一人便叫一声，师傅就开始包馍。人们看着稀奇，来买馍的也渐渐多了。
一日，一个江湖人见小猫伶俐，想要把它捉走。小猫就冲着师傅的方向嗷嗷大叫，师傅把手里的馍一丢，也不管对方是多么穷凶极恶的江湖人，就追了上去要猫。
好在江湖人讲道理，问师傅小猫叫什么。
它叫馍馍。跟着我一个做馍的，它就有饭吃；它帮我卖馍，我也有饭吃。
馍馍不明所以，但它飞快地攀上了师傅的肩头，再也不愿下来。
en:
One night, a weary vendor was closing his Rougamo stall.
"Out here in the middle of nowhere, who's going to eat my rougamo?" he sighed. A tiny "Meow?" came from his feet. A scruffy, palm-sized kitten looked up at him.
What harm could one little mouth do? He tossed it a scrap of meat. From that day on, the stall had a regular customer.
Soon, a strange thing happened: the village filled with wanderers, and the kitten would "meow" at each one, as if ordering a bun. Curious, they'd buy one. Business boomed.
One day, a rough-looking wanderer tried to snatch the kitten. The kitten yowled, and the vendor, without a second thought, chased after the man. "What's its name?" the man finally asked, impressed by the chase. "Rougamo," the vendor replied. "With a rougamo vendor for an owner, it'll never go hungry. And with it around, neither will I."
Rougamo, not understanding a word, scrambled up to its perch on the vendor's shoulder and refused to budge.

zh:
【某月廿二日】
墨门研学，忌虚谈废务，浮文妨要。
此番入世游历，按照门规，归来之日以本心创作机关一件，游学方有始终。
入世三月有余，蓝图一片空白，毫无头绪，愧对师长。
为平心中愁绪，亦为照拂百姓，近日投身汴梁东郊，重拾儿时务农之乐。

【某月廿四日】
榫卯机巧可解，而拖延之心不可解。
田野之间，烦恼全消。种地。

【某月廿六日】
不潜心研究机关为苍生谋福，单凭一人一犁，何以耕天下？
丘影啊丘影，何等堕落！

【次月一日】
幸得农家小儿赠东田瓜一枚。
田壤排水受滞，甜味不佳。若以机巧之力引渠分流，或有改善。
种地。

【次月三日】
偶遇同门故人闫舒。此人心高气傲，墨守亭中多次与我相辩，知错不改，活该唤作闫王。
问及归门机关，似已成竹在胸。
可气，可恼。不如种地。

【次月五日】
再逢闫王。
“丘兄既得务农之乐，何不以灌溉为题？”
信口胡言，不安好心。此话……
颇有几分道理？

【次月十日】
墨者之学，贵在务实。木料一根，可支梁柱；残革半片，可缝衣履。
引渠犁地，却少刃锋。闫王送百炼钢。磁州精铁而制，好钢，好钢。
此人往日嘲讽无状，难得良心发现。

【秋月十日】
不负师长教诲，引渠机巧初成，尚需与同门商议改进。
即日归山。
欠下人情一桩，也该向姓闫的道谢。竟是多日不见。

【冬月十二日】
再未见过闫舒。
手札交予入世同门，附信一封，若见此人，烦代为转交。
en:
[22nd Day of the Month]
Mohist studies abhor empty talk; superficial words only delay real progress.
For this worldly journey, sect rules dictate I must return with a mechanism created from my true calling to complete my training.
I have been in the world for over three months. My blueprints are completely blank. I have no ideas, and I bring shame to my masters.
To ease my troubled mind and help the locals, I have recently headed to the eastern suburbs of Bianliang to rediscover the joy of farming I knew as a child.

[24th Day of the Month]
Mechanical puzzles can be solved, but a procrastinating heart cannot.
In the fields, all my worries disappear.
I shall farm.

[26th Day of the Month]
If I don't focus on inventing mechanisms for the greater good, how can I plow the world with just one man and one plow?
Qiu Ying, Qiu Ying, what a slacker you've become!

[1st Day of the Next Month]
A farm boy kindly gave me a melon from the east field.
The soil here drains poorly, making the fruit bland. If I use mechanisms to divert water into irrigation channels, it might help.
I shall farm.

[3rd Day of the Next Month]
Bumped into Yan Shu, an old peer from the sect. The man is arrogant and stubborn. We debated endlessly back at the pavilion, and he never admits defeat. He truly earns his nickname, "Yama Yan," tyrant of the underworld.
When I asked about his final project, he looked entirely too confident.
Irritating. Infuriating.
I'm going back to farming.

[5th Day of the Next Month]
Ran into Yama Yan again.
"Since you enjoy farming so much, Brother Qiu, why not make irrigation your project?"
He was just spouting nonsense to mock me. And yet...
He has a point?

[10th Day of the Next Month]
Mohist learning values the practical. A single log can become a pillar; a scrap of leather can mend a boot.
For my irrigation plow, I lacked a proper blade. Yan sent me a piece of hundred-forged steel. Pure Cizhou iron. Excellent steel.
Given his usual endless sarcasm, a sudden bout of conscience is rare.

[10th Day of Autumn]
I have honored my masters' teachings. The prototype of the irrigation mechanism is done, though it needs peer review.
I head back to the mountain today.
I owe Yan a debt of gratitude and should thank him, but surprisingly, he has been nowhere to be found for days.

[12th Day of Winter]
I still haven't seen Yan Shu.
I'm passing this journal to a disciple heading down the mountain, along with a letter. If you run into him, please deliver it.
Xiang Ka

游侠，见字如面。
前些时日，老朽随府尹大人巡查蒙学，见学堂里的娃娃们一个个正襟危坐，埋首书卷，连我等走近了都未曾察觉。
老朽心下好奇，是何等妙文，能让这些上蹿下跳的娃娃们如此专心？一问才知，他们手中所读，竟是你前些时日所赠。
老朽又问，这些书好在何处？娃娃们七嘴八舌，老朽这才知道，原来你竟为每个孩子都择了不同的书，实在是费心了。而听闻老朽与你相熟，他们都央着我，定要代他们向你道声谢。
只是，真要问他们想说什么，这群小家伙却面露羞赧，讷讷而止了。最后，老朽想了个法子，让他们把想说的话都诉诸笔端，一并封在信里了。至于写了什么，老朽绝未偷看！
对了，娃娃们还托我转交几幅画作，说是读了书卷后的有感而发。他们都说，游侠你是他们见过最有眼光的人，定能欣赏他们的大作。
哈哈，看来往后若再有与孩子们打交道的差事，找游侠准是没错了。

en:
Dear Wanderer,

The other day, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the village school. The children sat straight at their desks, noses buried in scrolls, so absorbed they didn't even notice us draw near.
Curious what could hold their attention so completely, I asked. Turns out, they were reading the very books you gifted them not long ago.
I inquired further: what made these books so special? The little ones burst into chatter, and that's when I learned you had chosen a different book for each child. What thoughtfulness.
When they heard I knew you, they begged me to pass along their thanks.
But when I asked what they wanted to say, shyness took over, and words failed them. So I suggested they write it down instead. Their letters are enclosed. And no, I did not peek!
Oh, and they also asked me to send you a few drawings. Inspired, they said, by your books. They all agreed you're the most discerning person they've ever met, and that you'd surely appreciate their masterpieces.
Seems to me, whenever there's a task involving children, you're the one to call.

无忧边哭边东一句西一句地辩解着，倒让狄娟有些摸不着头脑了。那摊子虽小，可怎么着也是个正经分店。以后无忧就不是跑堂的帮工，而是狄家酒铺分铺的小老板了。
况且——
狄娟想起这姑娘自以为天衣无缝的“作案”手法，每天下班都强装镇定生怕谁看不出来要去做坏事，还有第二日衣裳上面残留的千日醉的香气……
她眉毛变得柔柔的，眼角弯弯，右手在柜台上支撑着下巴，就这么看着哭得喘不上气的万无忧。
小摊子上当日没卖完的千日醉，就归万无忧自己处理。
——这些打算，等晚点再和无忧说吧。
en:
The next morning, Di Juan called her to the counter. "You won't work inside the shop anymore," she said, not looking up. "I'm setting up a small stall along the road when folks get off work. You'll run it. It's closer to your home, and besides—"
She looked up and froze. Wuyou's eyes were already full of tears, like someone abandoned without warning.
"Waaah! Sister Di... I won't do it again..."
"I didn't mean to eavesdrop... and I only took a tiny jug, I haven't even finished half..."
"Please don't send me away... I'll change as you say, I swear..."
Between sobs and tangled explanations, Wuyou cried so hard. Di Juan didn't know whether to laugh or sigh. The stall might be small, but it was a proper branch of the business. From today on, Wuyou wouldn't be a helper, but a young keeper of the Di's Wine Shop.
Besides...
Di Juan remembered Wuyou's "perfect crimes"... The forced calm at the end of each shift, the barely hidden itch to misbehave, the faint trace of Sweet Slumber clinging to her clothes the next morning...
Her brows softened. Chin in hand, she just watched Wuyou sob and gasp, a smile curling the corners of her eyes.
Whatever wine was left over at the stall each day? That would be Wuyou's to "dispose of."
She'd tell her that later.

zh: 雷峰，在西湖南岸南屏山上。行及此处，多值黄昏，霞光映照，层林尽染，故曰雷峰夕照。 钱氏多筑塔，然宝塔非一朝一夕之功，虔心非一时一刻就。古有孟姜女哭长城，虔心既可成塔，不知来日，真情亦可使天崩塔裂乎？ 南屏山崖多有石刻，游人登山，见俯仰沉暮，心有戚戚焉，遂摩崖为记。斜阳之下，俱是行人，长歌归去，犹怀采薇。
en: Leifeng Tower stands atop Nanping Hill, on the southern shore of West Lake. Travelers who come here often arrive at dusk, when the glow of sunset bathes the forest in layered hues—hence its name, Sunset over Tower. The Qian clan built many pagodas, yet a pagoda is not the work of a single day, nor is devotion the labor of a single moment. Of old, Lady Meng Jiang's weeping brought down the Great Wall; if devotion alone could raise a pagoda, who is to say that true feeling, in days to come, might not likewise bring a tower crashing down? Upon the cliffs of Nanping Hill are carved many inscriptions, left by travelers who, gazing upon the fading dusk, felt their hearts stir with quiet sorrow, and so carved their thoughts into the rock. Beneath the slanting sun, all who pass are travelers, singing long as they turn homeward, hearts still lingering on gathered ferns of old.

zh:
亲爱的游侠们：

《燕云十六声》海外版本上线至今，已经陪伴大家走过半载。感谢大家在这半年里持续体验、反馈、讨论，也感谢大家愿意和我们一起把这片江湖慢慢建设得更好。

半周年期间，我们为大家准备了多项福利。希望这些心意，能为大家的半周年旅途添上一份纪念。

我们也清楚，大家最关心的，始终是游戏体验能否持续优化。
过去两个月里，我们根据海外玩家的集中反馈，已经在版本中落地了上百条优化与修复内容，包括装备养成专项优化、PVP专项优化、百业战开启时间调整为各地区当地时间，以及追赶系统、新手体验、PS端体验、手柄操作、聊天功能等多个模块的优化。
接下来，我们也会继续推进更多长期优化计划。针对服务器延迟问题，我们计划在澳洲、南美、中东增设服务器。针对新赛季武器平衡，我们会持续进行数据监控，在涉及数值调整时发布更清晰的公告，同时还将在7月开放「砺兵台·先琢」功能，各位游侠可参与新赛季前的平衡性测试并反馈建议。针对百业玩法内容，我们也将逐步增加更多自组织与GVE玩法。
对于大家长期关注的问题，我们也在持续推进中。包括许多关于希望“销金窟”在海外上线的呼声，由于全球各地区法律与合规环境存在差异，我们正在结合海外版本情况，评估更适合全球游侠体验的新系统方案，并会在后续同步更多进展。同时，我们也将持续投入移动端与PS端优化，逐步改善游戏在不同设备上的运行表现。
在后续版本中，皇宫区域即将开放，家业玩法、摸金玩法、伙伴系统、多人PVE玩法「武道心宫」、全新武器「手甲」，以及更多区域与休闲玩法，也将陆续与大家见面。更多详细内容，请关注《大鹅快报》半周年特别节目及后续官方公告。

再次感谢大家半年来的同行。江湖路远，相逢有幸；愿下一程，仍有新的风景、新的喜悦，也有更多值得我们一同期待的故事。
en:
Dear Wanderers,

Six months have passed since the global launch of Where Winds Meet. Thank you for spending this time with us, for playing, sharing your feedback, joining the discussions, and helping us make this jianghu a better place.

To celebrate this milestone, we have prepared a variety of special rewards. We hope these small tokens add a memorable touch to your journey.

We know what matters most to you is seeing the game continue to improve.

Over the past two months, we have listened closely to your feedback and shipped hundreds of fixes and improvements. These include targeted updates to gear progression and PvP, adjusting Guild War timers to match local server times, and a wide range of polish across the catch-up system, new player experience, PlayStation performance, controller support, and chat.

Looking ahead, we're rolling out several long-term improvements. To address server latency, we plan to add new servers in Australia, South America, and the Middle East. For weapon balance, we'll closely monitor the data and provide clearer patch notes whenever stat adjustments are made. In July, we'll also be opening Training Terrace – Preliminary, where players can participate in pre-season balance testing and share feedback. For Guilds, we'll gradually introduce more player-driven activities and GvE content.

We are also making progress on the long-term issues you care about most. We hear you on bringing the "Golden House" to the global version. Given how much legal and regulatory requirements vary across regions, we are currently designing a new system that delivers a great experience for Wanderers worldwide while remaining fully compliant. We will share more updates on this soon. We are also fully committed to continued optimization across mobile and PlayStation so the game runs well on all your devices.

In upcoming updates, the Imperial Palace region is opening soon! You can also look forward to new features rolling out gradually, including Homestead, Tomb Raiding, the Companion system, a new multiplayer PvE mode called "Martial Path Domain," the brand-new weapon Gauntlets, and an array of new regions and casual activities. Be sure to tune in to the Goose News Half-Anniversary Special and our official announcements for all the details.

Thank you once again for walking this path with us. The road through the jianghu is long, and we are incredibly fortunate to share it with you. As we ride toward the next horizon, may it bring new landscapes to explore, new joys to uncover, and many more stories to look forward to together.

2.【砂】的非凡奖励包括妆容【梦金墟】、耳饰【迟散金绮】和颈饰【迟散金绮】；【金】的非凡奖励包括头饰【迟散金绮】和发型【迟散金绮】；【曜】的非凡奖励包括服装【迟散金绮】和情境环境【沙海流晖】。
3.在【砂】、【金】和【曜】分别累计抽取次数，还可领取丰富奖励，包括主角头像【灵猫玄影】、题跋【仙人掌】、动态题跋【圣甲心】、置景【冥途引】、置景【悬衡秤心】和情景姿态【晓神意】。
4.敬请注意，集齐【迟散金绮】外观套件后，游侠可获赠结算演出【迟散金绮】和主角头像【迟散金绮】；【金乌瞳】在活动结束后将进行回收，无法继续使用。活动结束后，购买的【金乌瞳】将以16个兑换1个袅袅之音·绑进行系统回收，不足16个的【金乌瞳】将以1:10兑换为长鸣玉。
en:
1. Use Sun-Raven Eyes to draw for precious rewards, including the Aureate Dominion appearance set and the Shimmering Dunes scenario background. The first draw is free. Echo Jade and Echo Beads can also be exchanged for Sun-Raven Eyes (up to 18 Sun-Raven Eyes via Echo Jade). The event features 3 prize pools: Sand, Gold, and Radiance, each requiring different amounts of Sun-Raven Eyes per draw. Unlock all Epic rewards in the current pool to advance to the next. Each reward has a maximum acquisition limit; once reached, it will no longer be obtained, and its drop rate will be dynamically distributed among remaining rewards.
2. Epic rewards in the [Sand] pool include the Makeup: Gilded Mirage, Aureate Dominion: Earrings, and Aureate Dominion: Neckwear; Epic rewards in the [Gold] pool include Aureate Dominion: Headpiece and Aureate Dominion: Hairstyle; Epic rewards in the [Radiance] pool include Aureate Dominion: Outfit and the Scenario Background: Shimmering Dunes.
3. As your draw count increases separately in the [Sand], [Gold], and [Radiance] pools, you can also claim additional rewards, including the Player Avatar: Feline Phantom, Inscription: Desert Cactus, Dynamic Inscription: Scarab's Core, Decoration: Netherway Guide, Decoration: Heart Weigher, and Scenario Pose: Oracle Insight.
4. Please note: Collecting the complete Aureate Dominion appearance set grants the bonus Aureate Dominion victory cutscene and player avatar. Sun-Raven Eyes will be reclaimed after the event ends and can no longer be used. After the event ends, purchased Sun-Raven Eyes will be systematically converted at a rate of 16:1 into Lingering Melody: Bind. Any remaining Sun-Raven Eyes fewer than 16 will be converted into Echo Jade at a 1:10 ratio.

zh:
“富贵在天，死生有命。”养大石小石的男人常如此感慨。
“可我不信天，也不信命。”年幼的石小石常在心中反驳。
他自是不能信天，也不能信命。因为天命给了他最差的开局。他若是信了，便要永远深陷泥潭之中。

而那位来自商队的男人，真的给石小石带来了另一种天命的可能。
“机缘，是天与命的克星。”男人这般告诉石小石，“而赌石，便是你的机缘。”
从此石小石便跟着男人游走四方。但随着财富的滚滚而来，石小石渐渐明白，他们真正可用的机缘，其实是人心。

那些人心深处的细微渴望，只要从旁稍加引导，便自有要去的方向，便自能走向失控的终局。
这为石小石带来了无限的可能，也为他带来了无上的畅快。
那些高高在上的大人物，生来不会懂得浮萍野草的苦痛。他便要看着他们一朝倾覆，在泥潭间苦命挣扎。
而那些俯首偻行的小百姓……他也愿意从旁推他们一把，看他们飞上枝头，看他们逆天改命。
更多的时候，他笑看世人在欲望的淤泥中翻滚，他享受掌控他们命运的滋味。

富贵在天，死生有命。这一次，由他来做那个天，来改他们的命。
虽然他借了薛丑的地儿，承诺不会做的太过火。
但人心这玩意儿嘛，自有要去的方向，他不过从旁侧击，实在怨不得他什么……
en:
"Fortune lies in Heaven's hands. Life and death follow Fate's decree." The man who raised Shi Xiaoshi often sighed these words.
"But I believe in neither Heaven nor Fate," the young Shi Xiaoshi would silently retort.
He couldn't afford to believe, not when fate had dealt him the worst hand. To accept it would be to drown in the mire forever.

Then came the merchant caravan's man, offering a different kind of destiny.
"Opportunity is the bane of heaven and fate," the man told him. "And stone gambling is your opportunity." Thus, Shi Xiaoshi began traveling with the man. As wealth poured in, he realized their true "opportunity" lay in human hearts.

The slightest desires buried in men's hearts, when gently guided, would spiral out of control. 
This brought Xiaoshi endless possibilities and intoxicating power.
Nobles born to privilege could never understand the suffering of commoners. He delighted in watching them fall from grace, struggling in the mud of their own making.
As for the lowly peasants... he also liked to give them a push, to see them rise to glory, to defy their fate.
Mostly, he reveled in watching people wallow in the quagmire of desire, savoring the thrill of controlling their destinies.

"Fortune lies in Heaven's hands. Life and death follow Fate's decree." But now, he was the heaven, rewriting their fates.
True, he operated on Xue Chou's turf and promised not to overstep bounds.
But human hearts have a will of their own. He was merely guiding them, really. How could anyone blame him?

zh:
【文公第六】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。
继正即位，正也。
○二月，癸亥，日有食之。
○天王使叔服来会葬。
葬曰会，其志重天子之礼也。
○夏，四月，丁巳，葬我君僖公。
薨称公，举上也。葬我君，接上下也。僖公葬而后举谥，谥所以成德也，于卒事乎加之矣。
○天王使毛伯来锡公命。
礼有受命，无来锡命。锡命非正也。
○晋侯伐卫。
○叔孙得臣如京师。
○卫人伐晋。
○秋，公孙敖会晋侯于戚。
○冬，十月，丁未，楚世子商臣弒其君髠。
日髠之卒，所以谨商臣之弒也。夷狄不言正不正。
十公孙敖如齐。

二年，春，王二月，甲子，晋侯及秦师战于彭衙，秦师败绩。
○丁丑，作僖公主。
作，为也，为僖公主也。立主，丧主于虞，吉主于练。作僖公主，讥其后也。作主、坏庙，有时日于练焉。坏庙，坏庙之道，易檐可也，改涂可也。
○三月，乙巳，及晋处父盟。
不言公，处父伉也，为公讳也。何以知其与公盟？以其日也。何以不言公之如晋？所耻也。出不书，反不致也。
○夏，六月，公孙敖会宋公、陈侯、郑伯、晋士縠盟于垂陇。
内大夫可以会外诸侯。
○自十有二月不雨，至于秋七月。
历时而言不雨，文不忧雨也。不忧雨者，无志乎民也。
○八月，丁卯，大事于大庙，跻僖公。
大事者何？大是事也，着祫、尝。祫祭者，毁庙之主，陈于大祖，未毁庙之主，皆升合祭于大祖。跻，升也。先亲而后祖也，逆祀也。逆祀，则是无昭穆也。无昭穆则是无祖也，无祖则无天也。故曰文无天。无天者，是无天而行也。君子不以亲亲害尊尊，此春秋之义也。
○冬，晋人、宋人、陈人、郑人伐秦。
○公子遂如齐纳币。

……
en:
【Duke Wen, Sixth Year】

First year, spring, the king's first month, the Duke assumed the throne.
Succeeding to the rightful rule and assuming the throne is proper.
○In the second month, on the day Guihai, there was a solar eclipse.
○The Heavenly King sent Shufu to come and attend the funeral.
Attending a burial is called "hui" (to meet), and recording it emphasizes the importance of the Son of Heaven's rites.
○Summer, in the fourth month, on the day Ding Si, we buried our ruler, Duke Xi.
When a ruler dies, he is called "Duke," elevating his status. Burying our ruler connects the upper and lower ranks. After Duke Xi was buried, his posthumous name was then given; the posthumous name is used to complete his virtue, and it is added at the conclusion of the funeral rites.
○The Heavenly King sent Mao Bo to come and bestow upon the Duke a mandate.
According to ritual, there is receiving a mandate, but there is no coming to bestow a mandate. Bestowing a mandate in this way is not proper.
○The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei.
○Shusun Dechen went to the capital.
○The people of Wei attacked Jin.
○Autumn, Gongsun Ao met with the Marquis of Jin at Qi.
○Winter, in the tenth month, on the day Ding Wei, the Crown Prince of Chu, Shangchen, assassinated his ruler, Kun.
Recording the day of Kun's death is to carefully note Shangchen's assassination. For the barbarian tribes, one does not speak of proper or improper.
Gongsun Ao went to Qi.

Second year, spring, the king's second month, on the day Jiazi, the Marquis of Jin fought with the Qin army at Pengya, and the Qin army was defeated.
○On the day Ding Chou, the spirit tablet of Duke Xi was made.
"Making" means creating, creating the spirit tablet for Duke Xi. When establishing a spirit tablet, the mourning tablet is used during the yu sacrifice, and the auspicious tablet is used during the lian sacrifice. Making Duke Xi's spirit tablet criticizes that it was done too late. Making the spirit tablet and dismantling the shrine have their proper times, which are determined at the lian sacrifice. The way of dismantling a shrine is that replacing the eaves is acceptable, and repainting is also acceptable.
○In the third month, on the day Yi Si, [the Duke] made a covenant with Jin's Chufu.
The Duke is not mentioned because Chufu was arrogant, and it is to avoid embarrassment for the Duke. How do we know he made a covenant with the Duke? Because of the date. Why is it not mentioned that the Duke went to Jin? Because it was a humiliation. Going out is not recorded, and returning is not announced.
○Summer, in the sixth month, Gongsun Ao met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, and Jin's Shi Hu to make a covenant at Chuilong.
A high minister of our state may meet with feudal lords of other states.
○From the twelfth month there was no rain, until the seventh month of autumn.
Mentioning the lack of rain after such a long period indicates that Duke Wen did not worry about the rain. Not worrying about the rain means he had no concern for the people.
○In the eighth month, on the day Ding Mao, a great ceremony was held in the Grand Ancestral Temple, elevating Duke Xi.
What is the "great ceremony"? It is making this matter great, emphasizing the xia and chang sacrifices. In the xia sacrifice, the spirit tablets of destroyed shrines are displayed before the Grand Ancestor, and the spirit tablets of not-yet-destroyed shrines are all elevated and jointly sacrificed to the Grand Ancestor. "Ji" means to elevate. Placing the closer relative before the ancestor is a perverse sacrifice. A perverse sacrifice means there is no zhao-mu order. Without zhao-mu order, there is no ancestor; without an ancestor, there is no Heaven. Therefore it is said that Duke Wen had no Heaven. Having no Heaven means acting without Heaven. A noble person does not harm the reverence for the revered for the sake of closeness to kin; this is the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
○Winter, the people of Jin, Song, Chen, and Zheng attacked Qin.
○Gongsun Zi went to Qi to present betrothal gifts.

I once took slaughter as my trade, committing countless sins. As I grew older, I found myself unable to sleep at night and wished to draw my blade to end my own life. It so happened that a disciple of the Inkbound Order saw me and stayed my hand. He said to me, "You are a man of Qingzhou; why not learn the art of the culinary knife? To apologize with death leaves the sin uncleansed. It is better to cast aside the butcher's blade and take up the chef's knife; for every life nourished, a life is repaid."
I attained sudden enlightenment and thus established this precept: the descendants of the Sun clan shall never practice the arts of killing, but must solely use the culinary arts to save others. Trading the butcher's blade for the chef's knife is the true legacy of our Sun family. Whoever violates this is no true descendant of mine.

同道，你可听说墨山道盲审三大怪谈了？
异事有一，茫茫选海晕头转向，频频撞见一模一样的参选作品，唤作“鬼打墙”。
异事有二，作品质量无论高低，分数无论好坏，皆得票数，无有批判，唤作“混摸鱼”。
异事有三，下有瑟瑟发抖师兄师姐二人，上有鵙长老满头飞羽、背手吹须、焦灼踱步，唤作“成何体统”。
噫，今天全让我赶上了！
据说是前有粗心大意的师兄弄混了大家的盲审分组，后有负责誊录计分的师姐也犯了糊涂，气得长老把投票飞羽反手就扬了，在场一个不差地都落了满头。
但愿同道未被这些差池波及，还能秉持着大匠精神认真评审，将宝贵的飞羽投给真正潜心钻研的弟子。长老们之后将亲历亲为，一根一根羽毛认真计数，不会辜负大家的好点子的。
不过听鵙长老的弟子说，近来山野也有异事：
秋高气爽，进山训诫顽猴的人多了，那群野猴竟变得乖顺了起来，【小棘轮】都掉多了。
不过还望大家劳逸结合，免得把猴儿们训得讷然。鵙长老为此特意准备了不少 【小棘轮】和【长鸣玉】，助力大家的凿研大业。
话不多说，我也得继续努力去了，争取在下期的“投我一羽”上能让同道瞧见我的作品。共勉！
en:
Have you heard the Three Strange Tales of Mohist Hill's Blind Review?
Tale One: Reviewers drown in a sea of repeats. Called "Ghost Walls."
Tale Two: All works get votes, no critique. Called "Muddled Fishing."
Tale Three: Two terrified juniors below; Elder Shrike pacing above, muttering "Utterly improper!"
I witnessed all three today!
A careless senior mixed up review groups; the scoring senior sister muddled records. And in fury, Elder Shrike scattered the voting feathers, showering everyone.
Hope you stay untouched, judging with skill, and casting feathers for true disciples. The elders will count each feather now, so good ideas won't go to waste.
But here's another strange thing according to Elder Shrike's disciples: more people training monkeys have made them docile. [Small Ratchets] drop more often!
But don't overdo it, lest the monkeys grow dull. Elder Shrike has stocked up on [Small Ratchets] and [Echo Jade] to fuel the work.
Back to work. Hope my piece makes the next "Cast Me a Feather." Onward!

zh:
《汉书》有云，“骏马名骓。”骓，指毛色苍白相间。吐谷浑马中有此纹理者，为青骓。
相传秦时甘陇一带产良马，时称“秦马”。西汉景帝年间，在西北边郡设马苑，养秦马万千，后有吐谷浑人驻牧。《隋书》有云：“吐谷浑有青海，中有小山。其俗至动辄方牝马与其上，言其龙种。尝得波斯草马放入海，因生骢驹，日行千里。”书中所云骢驹即为“吐谷浑马”。
吐谷浑马骨充肌丰，体躯舒展，健而有力，温顺易驯。喜群居，好游走，群马中必有公马为首。耳聪目明，性机敏，记心强，同类相惜，认主不忘。可乘骑，可轻挽，为中原最常见的马种。
en:
The Book of Han states: "A fine steed is called a zhui", referring to horses with intermingled white and gray hair. Among the Tuyuhun Horses, those with such markings were known as Qingzhui - Azure-Gray Charger. 
Legend holds that during the Qin dynasty, the fertile lands of Ganlong produced exceptional steeds known as "Qin Horse." In the reign of Emperor Jing of the Western Han, a vast imperial stud farm was founded in the northwest to raise thousands of these horses. Later, the Tuyuhun people came to pasture here. The Book of Sui recounts: "Tuyuhun lies near Qinghai, where stands a small sacred hill. They believe dragons mate with mares atop it, thus their horses are of dragon blood. It's said a Persian grass-fed stallion once swam across the sea, and sired a dappled colt that ran a thousand miles a day." This legendary colt is known as the Tuyuhun Horse. 
Broad of chest and smooth of frame, the Tuyuhun Horse is powerful, yet gentle and easy to tame. Fond of roaming in herds, it always follows a lead stallion. With keen ears and sharp eyes, it is intelligent and loyal, and bonding closely with its kin. It is well-suited for riding and light draft work, and is among the most common breeds in the Central Plains.

墨家学说创立者，以摹略万物理、精研机关术而著称。墨学在先秦影响深远，有“非儒即墨”之说。
墨子亡故后，墨家一分为三。其一于西汉初年隐于不见山，定千年之计，称墨山道。
世人皆传，墨子崇理而严正，但在墨山道留存的记载中，却时有“工于机关尤善制鸢，门中孩童人手一只”，“与公输班辩理，兴之所至三日不歇”，之类的趣闻。
en:
Mozi, founder of the Mohist school, was renowned for his grasp of the principles underlying all things and for his mastery of mechanical arts. His teachings held great influence in the pre-Qin era, giving rise to the saying, "One follows either Confucianism or Mohism."

After his death, the Mohist school split into three branches. In the early Western Han, one branch withdrew into Hidden Mountain and laid plans for a thousand years to come. This branch became known as Mohist Hill.

Mozi is often remembered as a stern man devoted to reason, yet the records preserved by Mohist Hill reveal a more lively side: tales of his skill in crafting eagles, enough for every child in the order to have one, and of debates with Gongshu Ban that went on for three days without pause.

不过倒是不撞不相识，我跟着此处的村民相处了好几日，这些高转筒车借助水力便能动，还有那麦笼麦绰实在有趣，我可帮了她们做了不少农活！腰——酸——背——疼——不过，他们送给我的吃食味道实在不错。
她们说前头的承恩镇里还有百合面、通神饼，最近还正逢社日，等我吃完这张烤饼，我就要往那边去啦！
老天保佑，可别又迷路了！
en:
Lost, lost again! 
Left is wheat, right is wheat, front is wheat, back is wheat too! How am I supposed to tell north from south? Whoosh—there are always people sleeping in the wheat field day and night. I couldn't see clearly at night and stepped on someone by accident. She yelled "ghost," and I yelled "ghost" too. What a damned mess! 
But it's a funny way to make friends. I've stayed with the local villagers for days. Their high-rotation waterwheels move with water power, and those wheat baskets and sickles are so interesting! I helped them with loads of farm work—my back is killing me! But the food they gave me tasted amazing. 
They said Gracetown ahead serves Lily Bulb Noodles and Scallion Pancake. It's also Community Festival time! After finishing this baked pancake, I'm heading there. 
Heaven help me, don't let me get lost again!

定音自选无需消耗变音材料，只能自选词条类型，选定后词条数值会按照变音规则随机生成。

en:
Gear at Tier 81 and above can be retuned and re-attuned after it has been attuned.
Select a preferred Path, consume a Retuning Stone to gain a random new Attribute from that Path's recommended library. The new Attribute will not be the same as the old one. Quality Guaranteed Materials can be added.
One Attribute can be retuned at most per piece of gear. Initial Attributes cannot be retuned. Gear at Tier 105 can further re-tune a retuned Attribute with no limit on attempts, but there is a cooldown between each re-retune. When re-retuning, any Attributes from the same Retuning Library that have been gained from previous retune attempts will not appear again.
Gear with an initial tier of 110 unlocks Relaid Retuning and the Historical Retuning Library.

Regular and Arena Attunement can be performed simultaneously, but only one can be active at a time. Switching between them is free.
After selecting an Attuning Library, consume Attunement Stones and Re-attunement Stones to gain a random new Attribute from the corresponding library.
The new Attribute may be the same. You may choose whether to overwrite the old Attribute. Unselected Attributes are stored in the re-attuning Library and can be re-enabled by spending 20 Echo Jade.
If the same Attribute as the current one gets rolled from re-attuning, the value is guaranteed to increase.

Once Gear at Tier 100 accumulates a certain number of re-attuning attempts, you will have a chance to select an attunement of your choice. Common Attunement and Arena Attunement counts are tracked independently per piece of gear.
The attunement selection does not consume re-attuning materials. The Attribute type can be selected, but the Attribute value will be randomly generated according to rules.
Converting a piece of gear to Relaid Gear will reset the re-attuning pity count.

zh:
【子路第十三】

子路问政。子曰：“先之，劳之。”请益，曰：“无倦。”
仲弓为季氏宰，问政。子曰：“先有司，赦小过，举贤才。”曰：“焉知贤才而举之？”曰：“举尔所知，尔所不知，人其舍诸？”
子路曰：“卫君待子而为政，子将奚先？”子曰：“必也正名乎！”子路曰：“有是哉，子之迂也！奚其正名？”子曰：“野哉，由也！君子于其所不知，盖阙如也。名不正，则言不顺。言不顺，则事不成。事不成，则礼乐不兴。礼乐不兴，则刑罚不中。刑罚不中，则民无所措手足。故君子名之必可言也，言之必可行也，君子于其言，无所苟而已矣。”
樊迟请学稼，子曰：“吾不如老农。”请学为圃。子曰：“吾不如老圃。”樊迟出。子曰：“小人哉，樊须也！上好礼，则民莫敢不敬。上好义，则民莫敢不服。上好信，则民莫敢不用情。夫如是，则四方之民襁负其子而至矣，焉用稼？”
子曰：“诵诗三百，授之以政，不达。使于四方，不能专对。虽多，亦奚以为哉？”
子曰：“其身正，不令而行；其身不正，虽令不从。”
子曰：“鲁卫之政，兄弟也。”
子谓卫公子荆，“善居室。始有，曰：‘苟合矣。少有’，曰：‘苟完矣。’富有，曰：‘苟美矣。’”
子适卫，冉有仆。子曰：“庶矣哉。”冉有曰：“既庶矣，又何加焉？”曰：“富之。”曰：“既富矣，又何加焉？”曰：“教之。”
子曰：“苟有用我者，期月而已可也。三年有成。”
子曰：“善人为邦百年，亦可以胜残去杀矣。诚哉，是言也。”
子曰：“如有王者，必世而后仁。”
子曰：“苟正其身矣，于从政乎何有？不能正其身，如正人何？”
冉子退朝。子曰：“何晏也？”对曰：“有政。”子曰：“其事也。如有政，虽不吾以，吾其与闻之。”
定公问：“一言而可以兴邦，有诸？”孔子对曰：“言不可以，若是其几也。”人之言曰：‘为君难，为臣不易。’如知为君之难也，不几乎一言而兴邦乎？”曰：“一言而可丧邦，有诸？”孔子对曰：“言不可以若是其几也。”人之言曰：‘予无乐乎为君，唯其言而乐，莫予违也。’如其善而莫之违也，不亦善乎？如不善而莫之违也，不几乎一言而丧邦乎？”
叶公问政，子曰：“近者悦，远者来。”
子夏为莒父宰，问政。子曰：“毋欲速，毋见小利。欲速，则不达。见小利，则大事不成。”
叶公语孔子曰：“吾党有直躬者，其父攘羊，而子证之。”孔子曰：“吾党之直者异于是。父为子隐，子为父隐，直在其中矣。”

en:
【Book XIII: Zilu】

Zilu asked about governance. The Master said: "Lead them, and then labor them." When asked for more advice, he said: "Do not grow weary."
Zhonggong, serving as steward to the Ji family, asked about governance. The Master said: "Set an example for your officials, pardon minor faults, and promote the worthy and talented." When asked, "How can one recognize the worthy and talented to promote them?" he replied: "Promote those you know. As for those you do not know, will others neglect them?"
Zilu said: "If the ruler of Wei were to await you to govern, what would you prioritize?" The Master said: "It would have to be the rectification of names!" Zilu said: "Is that so? How pedantic you are! Why rectify names?" The Master said: "How uncultivated you are, You! A gentleman, regarding what he does not know, maintains a reserved attitude. If names are not rectified, speech will not be in accord. If speech is not in accord, affairs will not be accomplished. If affairs are not accomplished, rites and music will not flourish. If rites and music do not flourish, punishments will not be just. If punishments are not just, the people will have nowhere to place their hands and feet. Therefore, a gentleman must be able to speak of what he names, and what he speaks must be practicable. A gentleman, in his speech, leaves nothing to carelessness."
Fan Chi asked to learn farming. The Master said: "I am not as good as an old farmer." He asked to learn gardening. The Master said: "I am not as good as an old gardener." Fan Chi left. The Master said: "What a petty man Fan Xu is! If those above love ritual, none among the people will dare be disrespectful. If those above love righteousness, none among the people will dare be disobedient. If those above love trustworthiness, none among the people will dare be insincere. If it is thus, the people from all quarters will come carrying their children on their backs. What need is there for farming?"
The Master said: "One who has recited the three hundred odes, yet when entrusted with governance cannot carry it out, or when sent on missions to the four quarters cannot respond independently—though he has learned much, of what use is it?"
The Master said: "If a man is correct in his own conduct, he will be followed without orders being given. If he is not correct in his own conduct, he will not be obeyed even if orders are given."
The Master said: "The governance of Lu and Wei are like brothers."
The Master said of Prince Jing of Wei: "He was good at managing a household. When he first had something, he said: 'This is barely adequate.' When he had a little more, he said: 'This is barely complete.' When he had plenty, he said: 'This is barely splendid.'"
When the Master went to Wei, Ran You drove for him. The Master said: "How populous it is!" Ran You said: "Since it is populous, what more should be done?" He said: "Enrich them." He said: "Once they are enriched, what more should be done?" He said: "Educate them."
The Master said: "If anyone were to employ me, in a year it would be possible, and in three years there would be accomplishment."
The Master said: "If good men were to govern a state for a hundred years, they could also overcome cruelty and eliminate killing. How true this saying is!"
The Master said: "If a true king were to arise, it would take a generation for benevolence to prevail."
The Master said: "If a man can rectify himself, what difficulty is there in governing? If he cannot rectify himself, how can he rectify others?"
Master Ran returned from court. The Master said: "Why so late?" He replied: "There were affairs of governance." The Master said: "They were merely routine matters. If there were affairs of governance, though I am not employed, I would have heard of them."
Duke Ding asked: "Is there a single saying that can make a state prosper?" Confucius replied: "A saying cannot be like that, but there is one that comes close. People say: 'It is difficult to be a ruler, and not easy to be a minister.' If one understands the difficulty of being a ruler, is that not close to a saying that can make a state prosper?" He asked: "Is there a single saying that can ruin a state?" Confucius replied: "A saying cannot be like that, but there is one that comes close. People say: 'I take no pleasure in being a ruler, except that no one opposes my words.' If his words are good and no one opposes them, is that not good? If his words are not good and no one opposes them, is that not close to a saying that can ruin a state?"
The Duke of She asked about governance. The Master said: "Make those near happy, and those far away will come."
Zixia, serving as steward of Jufu, asked about governance. The Master said: "Do not desire speed, do not look for small gains. If you desire speed, you will not attain your goal. If you look for small gains, great affairs will not be accomplished."
The Duke of She said to Confucius: "In my village there is a man named Straight Body. His father stole a sheep, and the son bore witness against him." Confucius said: "The straight men in my village are different from this. The father conceals for the son, and the son conceals for the father. Straightness lies within this."

zh: ，甘泉入户，今有余泽。移船湖北，湖光如镜，芙蓉千叠，有长堤横卧如玉带，四围石砌，道中铺沙，夹种桃柳。此乐天相公所遗，“绿杨阴里白沙堤”也。仰观则又有峰岫峥嵘，幽僻出尘，唤作葛岭，晋人抱朴子葛洪炼丹于此。继而转西，苍山交横，流泉千缕。下饮平湖，上接云脚，郁郁葱葱，如浮屠展臂，灵隐诸峰也。诗仙太白曾游其间，有“天竺森在眼，松风飒惊秋。览云测变化，弄水穷清幽”之诗。
en: . Even now, that sweet spring water nourishes the common folk, a blessing that has outlasted empires. As we drifted north, the lake smoothed into a sheet of glass, dappled with unfurling lotus blossoms. A long causeway spanned the water like a ribbon of carved jade. Paved with sand, bordered by stone, and sheltered by peach blossoms and weeping willows, this was the White Sand Causeway. It is the very path bequeathed to us by Bai Juyi, immortalized in his verse: "The white sand causeway veiled in the shade of weeping willows." Raising our eyes, we beheld soaring, ethereal peaks that seemed entirely untethered from the mortal world. This was Ge Ridge, where the alchemist Ge Hong once forged his alchemical elixirs. Drifting further west unveiled a rich tapestry of overlapping emerald slopes and winding streams. Spring water cascaded from the heights to meet the placid lake, while the verdant ridges stretched out like the welcoming arms of a grand stupa. These were the peaks of Lingyin. When the Poet Immortal, Li Bai, wandered through these very hills, he wrote: "Tianzhu's deep forests rise before my eyes, as sighing pine winds wake the autumn skies. I watch the shifting clouds to fathom how they sweep and trace the quiet waters, still and deep."

zh:
太平钟楼下，敲钟老人的箫声依旧。你的到来并未打断他的闲情。箫声一转，如泣如诉。你不是第一次来到这里，但这一次，你似乎听出了曲中的故事。那是汤汤洛水与皓皓白雪的交锋，是凛冽寒梅与清澈深泉的对望，是一对恋人变作怨侣的转折，是情与义落下至真至痛的一笔，是从此天涯陌路人的诀别。你知道故事里的人是谁，可那场大战她从没对你提起，你也不知最后是谁赢了。老人似乎看出你所想，将同样的问题抛给了你。你思索片刻，回答道……
⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛
老人微笑，不置可否。他向你缓缓讲述着故事的余料。悬剑之义，天泉之义，洛神之义，燕北盟之义……每个人都站在了道义的箭锋之上，而引弦之手，从不由人。
en:
Beneath the Peace Bell Tower, the old bell-ringer's flute still sings as ever. Your arrival does nothing to disturb his quiet ease. Then the melody shifted, weeping and whispering like a grief too deep for words. This is not your first time here, yet this time, you seem at last to hear the story hidden within the song.
It is the clash between the surging Luo River and the gleaming white snow; the silent gaze between bitter winter plum and a deep, clear spring. It is the turning point where lovers become estranged, the stroke where love and duty leave their truest, most agonizing mark, the final parting that leaves them as strangers at the ends of the earth. You know who the story is about. Yet she has never spoken of that great battle, and you never learned who emerged victorious in the end. The old man seems to read your thoughts, tossing the same question back to you. After a moment's reflection, you give your answer...

The old man only smiles, neither confirming nor denying it. Slowly, he recounts the untold fragments of the tale: the honor of the Hanging Blade, the honor of Well of Heaven, the honor of Water Lady, the honor of the Northern Vow… Each stood balanced upon the arrowhead of honor, yet the hand that drew the bowstring was never their own.

zh:
“乱世命如草芥，为何不肯握住这长生机缘？”
徐文清不懂。他将改制好的春蚕捧给妻儿看。于是当夜，妻子便带着孩子连夜逃走了。
后来他在深山寻到两具枯骨。白骨上静静息着一大一小两只飞蛾。
他笑着轻唤：“春娘，阿苗，是我啊。”
飞蛾一动不动。
他有些急了，声音发颤：“是阿爹啊。”
死寂。
他终于快要哭了：“春娘！阿苗！过来啊！”
两只蛾子动了，飞过来，朝他——或者只是本能扑向活物，或者漫无目的、朝天飞去，但都不要紧。
虫躯像微笑一样蠕动。他张开双臂。
en:
"Life is cheaper than weeds in this age of chaos. Why throw away a chance at immortality?"
Xu Wenqing simply couldn't understand. He proudly showed the mutated spring silkworms to his family. That very night, his terrified wife took their child and fled into the dark.
Much later, deep in the mountains, he found two sets of withered bones. Resting silently on the remains were two moths: one large, the other small.
He smiled and called out softly, "Chunniang, Miao... It's me."
The moths didn't move.
Panic set in, his voice trembling. "It's Papa."
Dead silence.
Finally, on the verge of breaking down, he cried out, "Chunniang! Miao! Come to me!"
The two moths stirred. They flew toward him, perhaps merely acting on some blind instinct to attack a living creature, or maybe just fluttering aimlessly into the air. It didn't matter.
Their segmented bodies writhed in a grotesque semblance of a smile. He opened his arms to embrace them.

en:
They say a single day as husband and wife fosters a hundred days of grace. I was truly fortunate to have met you, my lord, to be wed in the warmth of spring, our fates bound as I came of age.

Yet our noble house fell in a single night. I intended to follow you, to shatter like jade, but word came from Hexi that you had cast me aside.
I know too well that your cold words of release were a shield to grant me life.

In this life, we may never meet again. Therefore, I must blaze a trail through this wasteland, carving out a chance at survival from this utter despair. Only then can I honor the sacrifice you made for me.

Reflecting on this life, I have crossed seas of sand and shouldered great responsibilities. If we should meet again in the Yellow Springs, I swear you will see me with new eyes.

Our fate in this world was brief, yet I pray for the next. I hold no regrets. May you always know this.

zh:
她初至梨园，先见到一片桃花林，听到一阵乐声。

桃夭灼灼，她在树与花的迷阵里不知方向，只能循着乐声往深处走。往深处走，人影渐明。她低头避开一根枝桠，抬头时春风拂面，有舞者如一片落英翩然飞到她的面前。

“你会唱歌吗？”舞者问。
“会一点。”
“那来给我伴唱吧！”

舞者捉着她的手腕往台上跑，足尖一点就飞到枝头。
“来呀！唱！”

她茫然地开口，舞者随她的歌声扬袖旋身，于花树间轻盈徘徊。花与人，人与花，交织成绮丽的梦影。
于是她迟疑的歌声唱得越来越定、越来越亮，和舞者的步履宛转相合。

一曲终了。她尚且怔愣，舞者已经蝴蝶般投入她怀中，笑道：“我喜欢你！你叫什么名字？”
“我入梨园，是为了抛却过往……就叫白新。”
“刚取的吗？真好听！我叫阿朱，待你入门，来跟我合演好不好？”
“……好。”

这是她们合演的第一曲，唯有天地山水看见。
很快，就有了第二曲、第三曲……越来越多的人看见她们的歌舞，越来越多的人喜欢她们的歌舞。
阿朱的舞以繁复华美为要，她的歌以轻灵无垢称道，合演之时，既是彼此互补，又是默契天成。梨园内遂称她们为一时双璧。

园中舞乐不休，岁月白驹在技艺精研中奔驰得飞快。
第二年春天，她们在相遇的桃花树下埋了一坛酒，约定冬日再来启封。
夏蝉鸣叫的时候，她们各自遇到了技艺的瓶颈。
秋季的某一日，阿朱飞到她窗前，眼神明亮地说：“我想到了！我想到要如何突破如今的困境了！”
“舞是世间万千生灵共通的话语。倘若没有见过世间的万千生灵如何在山河间漫游，我怎么能够舞出其中的神韵呢？我决定了，我要到外面去。去见山、见水、见众生！”
“你要随我一起走吗？”

“不了。”她摇摇头，“世间百声繁杂，会有碍我想表达的声音。”

她的蝴蝶飞走了。
但她并不伤心。
她觉得相遇与重逢都是理所应当的事情，告别之后，自然会有重聚。谁也没有觉得不舍。她们理应走上自己认定的道路，成为更好的人以后重逢，再一起完成更完美的歌舞。

直到有一日，新进的弟子问她，“您有见过朱大家的舞吗？朱大家以舞姿纷繁、如揽万象于舞中而闻名；您的歌喉则纯澈灵粹、脱俗于世外，若能乐舞同台，一定会像两块碧玉一样相映成辉！”
她才恍然惊觉，已经有许多许多年，没有见过阿朱了。

她去找当年埋的春酒，却遍寻不到一片桃夭灼灼的花林。
梨园当真有一片桃花林吗？还是那一日的记忆太鲜妍，以至于也为记忆中的花卉着色？
她不记得了。甚至不记得，是否真有那样一个蝴蝶般的人、一场如梦般的歌舞。
那一日的天与地、山和水还记得吗？

她去沽了一壶酒，一人两杯，望着天边的行云饮完了。
en:
When she first stepped into the Masked Troupe, her eyes were greeted by a blooming grove of peach trees, and soft music floated through the air. 

Amid the radiant blossoms, she found herself lost in a labyrinth of petals and branches, unsure of the way—but she followed the melody deeper into the grove. As she ventured further, shadows of figures began to emerge. Bending to dodge a low-hanging branch, she looked up just as a spring breeze brushed her cheek, and a dancer, as light and graceful as falling petals, twirled down to meet her. 

"Can you sing?" the dancer asked with a smile. 
"A little." 
"Then sing with me." 

Seizing her wrist, the dancer led her toward the stage, then, with a delicate tap of toes, soared onto a branch above. 
"Come on! Sing!" 

At first hesitant, her voice gradually grew steadier and clearer, weaving seamlessly with the dancer's flowing movements. Between the blossoms and their intertwined forms, the two became a living dream of music and motion. 
Her tentative melody blossomed into a confident, radiant song, perfectly echoing the dancer's elegant steps. 

When the final note faded, she was still caught in the moment, while the dancer, fluttering like a butterfly, leapt into her arms and laughed, "I like you! What's your name?" 
"I came to the Masked Troupe to leave my past behind... Call me Bai Xin." 
"Did you just choose that? It's beautiful. I'm A'zhu. When you officially join, will you perform with me?" 
"...Yes." 

Their first duet was witnessed only by the sky, the earth, and the murmuring mountains. 
Soon came a second, then a third... and more and more people gathered to behold and be enchanted by their singing and dancing. 
A'zhu's dance dazzled with intricate grace and brilliance; Bai Xin's voice shimmered with lightness and purity. Together, their performances were a perfect harmony of contrast and complement—so natural it seemed destined. They were celebrated in the Masked Troupe as an unparalleled pair. 

Music and dance filled the garden day and night, and the years swiftly passed as their artistry deepened. 
The following spring, beneath the very peach tree where they first met, they buried a jar of wine, promising to return and open it together when winter came again. 
When the summer cicadas sang their endless chorus, both of them found themselves trapped in the stubborn grip of a creative block. 
One crisp autumn day, A'zhu appeared at her window, eyes bright with sudden realization. "I've figured it out! I know how to break free from this rut!" 
"Dance is the universal language of all living things. Without witnessing the countless creatures that roam the mountains and rivers, how could I ever capture their spirit in my movement? I've made up my mind—I must go beyond these walls. I'll see the landscape and all the living souls out there!" 
"Will you come with me?" 

"No," she answered softly, shaking her head. "The world is filled with clamorous sounds that would drown out the voice I'm trying to hear." 

And with that, her butterfly took flight and vanished on the breeze. 
Yet she felt no sorrow. 
To her, meetings and partings were natural cycles, inevitable and necessary. Farewells only made reunions sweeter. There was no room for clinging; each was meant to walk the path their heart knew best—to become more fully themselves—until they could once again join in song and dance, more perfect than ever before. 

Then one day, a new disciple asked her, "Have you ever seen Master Zhu's dance? She weaves the universe itself into her movements. Your voice, pure and transcendent, soars beyond the everyday. If your music and her dance graced the same stage, it would be like two jade gems reflecting each other's brilliance." 
It was then she realized with a pang—how many long years had passed since she last saw A'zhu? 

She returned to the place where they'd buried their spring wine, but found no sign of the radiant peach grove they once called home. 
Did the Masked Troupe ever truly bloom with peach blossoms? Or had that day's memory simply painted its own dreamlike flowers? 
She no longer knew. She couldn't say if there had ever truly been that butterfly-like figure, or that ethereal song and dance. 
But perhaps the sky and earth remembered—the mountains and rivers. 

She bought a jar of wine, poured two cups, and raising them to the drifting clouds on the horizon, drank alone—a quiet toast to what was, and what might still be.
An off-white seat cushion.

zh: 若闻花毽魁主威名，当识得降龙寨主祝英晗，岂有他哉？ 眉眼带煞，英气冲天。风雨愈急，其势愈张。 桃李之年，已识刀光剑影，为众匪率首。 昔时青州，恶匪如泥蛟，横行一方，气焰甚炽。 英晗随其姊英琦入山，径叩匪巢，以擒龙之势，连败匪首。自此，黑龙遁海，山寨易帜。 未料日前，英琦因事离寨，延请友人狄诚暂代寨务。英晗岂肯低眉顺目，俯首帖耳，遂以花毽较技，定寨主之位。 空山之中，锣鼓渐起，忽一毽高飞入云，迟迟不落。众人仰首，唯见白云悠悠，山色苍茫，不知羽毽，终究落入谁手……
en:
To speak of the Shuttlecock Champion is to speak of Zhu Yinghan, Chief of Dragonfall Camp. Truly, who else could it be? There is menace in her eyes and heroic fire in her bearing. The harder the wind and rain, the more fiercely her spirit rises. Barely twenty years of age, she is already a seasoned veteran of blade and blood, leading a mountain of outlaws.
There was a time when vicious bandits ran rampant across Qingzhou like serpents in the mire. Yinghan and her elder sister, Yingqi, marched straight into the mountains, striking at the heart of the lair and crushing the bandit lords like tamers of dragons. From then on, the Black Dragon fled to the sea, and the stronghold changed hands.
Recently, however, Yingqi left the camp on urgent matters, leaving her trusted friend Di Cheng as acting chief. How could Yinghan ever bow to another? Thus, a duel of shuttlecock was called to decide who truly rules the stronghold.
In the empty mountains, the drums begin to roll. Suddenly, a feathered shuttlecock flies high into the clouds and does not fall. All look up, seeing only drifting white clouds and vast mountain slopes, with no way of knowing whose hand it will finally descend into...

Two names: Cheng Youjing, Hang Tiantian. 
Traces left by a pair of lovers in a well tunnel—each inscription written side by side. 
Between digging, they secretly etched their names everywhere. The other would find it and add their beloved's name. 
A simple game, like the bow they imagined exchanging as husband and wife. These names, under heaven and earth, forever paired. 

Before leaving on a camel adorned with red flowers, the girl wrote one last inside the well. 
Sold by her father to a merchant caravan—they could take her far away. Where there was water, a better life. 
But she wept. That faraway place had no boy whose name she wrote.

山魈篇
《抱朴子·登涉》云：山精形如小儿，独足向后，夜喜犯人，名曰魈。
此怪生于深山，手足加之，仅有三肢，然力大无穷。

徐铉书载：“……舒州有山鬼，善为此厉。盖黎丘之徒也。” 
此鬼极善幻化，常化作命主至亲至近之人，或作老妪，或作童子，趁夜色深重，叩门入室，以假乱真。

近鬼者，必有殒命之忧。山魈喜日夜尾随，步步紧逼，以惧养怨。 
初时闻院外有独足跳跃之声，若兽绕墙而行。十日往后，登堂入室，鬼疮绕臂，是为鬼作。

至第十四日夜半，山魈勒命主脖颈，使其口不能呼，手不能挣，窒息而亡。
en:
Xu Xuan, a learned scholar of the Kingdom of Jiangnan, compiled strange accounts from across the land in his Records of Spirits.
This anthology combines stories I gathered on my travels with the most dangerous, verified cases from Xu Xuan's work. These are no idle tales.

The Mountain Demon
The chapter "Entering the Mountains" in Alchemical Codex describes a mountain spirit resembling a small child, with a single backward-facing foot. It attacks people at night and is known as the xiao.
Found deep in the mountains, this creature has only three limbs, yet possesses tremendous strength.

Xu Xuan writes: "...A mountain ghost in Shu Prefecture is particularly skilled in such mischief. It appears to be kin to the spirits of Liqiu."
A gifted shapeshifter, it often takes the form of someone close to its victim. Disguised as an old woman or a child, it knocks at the door late at night and gains entry, its disguise all but impossible to see through.

Anyone who encounters one is in mortal danger. The mountain demon follows its victim day and night, creeping ever closer and feeding on their fear.
At first, a single hopping foot can be heard outside the courtyard, like an animal circling the walls. After ten days, the creature enters the house. Sores appear around the victim's arm, a mark of its presence.

At midnight on the fourteenth day, it grips the victim by the throat. Unable to cry out or struggle, the victim suffocates.

 · #Y落地性#Y评分，代表此作品是否具有可拓展的空间、是否可以造福桃园。

en:
Waterworks Masters may submit #YScenic Landmarks containing construction data#E for fellow disciples to review and vote on, determining the next Great Mohists. Works are assessed across four categories:
- #YInnovation#E: Measures how original and groundbreaking the design is.
- #YFeasibility#E: Evaluates whether the design can be put into practice and how it may benefit the Haven.
- #YCompleteness#E: Reflects the overall level of refinement and completion. Please evaluate the work as a whole.
- #YSustainability#E: Represents the Mohist belief that creation should evolve with the times, maintaining harmony between people, nature, and the ecosystem. Construction must not occupy animal habitats, water sources, and other natural areas.

zh:
阿郎降生的那天，万雁躺在床上幸福地擦着眼泪。
剧痛尚未散去，但她已经迫不及待从稳婆手里接过啼哭的婴孩。
“儿啊，阿娘……谢谢你。”
“谢谢你选择我做你的阿娘。谢谢你愿意通过我，来到这世上。”
万雁暗暗想，她一定要给孩子自由而快乐的一生。

从小，万雁都不愿给孩子一点委屈。
不是说万雁舍不得苛责阿郎——孩子的长大总需要立规矩。万雁从不把不应加诸孩儿的期望压在他身上。相比于别人家的爷娘成天唠叨着望子成龙之类的话语，万雁最常说的便是“阿娘听你的。”
她一开始就知道，她的孩子不属于她，而是属于他自己。他愿意降生在自己膝下喊一声阿娘，这便是几世的福气。

万雁信佛，未出阁之时便常常于佛前供灯。
有了阿郎以后，万雁便会多为孩子单独供一盏，以阿郎的名义。
“儿啊，阿娘帮你供灯，但你要知道，你的今后的荣华，都是你自己的造化。”
“以后你要飞走的时候，就不必眷着娘。”
“但只要你累了，阿娘永远为你留着家。”
en:
The day A'Lang was born, Wan Yan lay in bed, happily wiping away tears. 
The searing pain hadn't yet faded, but she couldn't wait to take the wailing infant from the midwife's hands 
"My child... thank you." 
"Thank you for choosing me as your mother. Thank you for being willing to come into this world through me." 
Wan Yan silently vowed she would give this child a life of freedom and joy. 

From infancy, Wan Yan was unwilling to let her child suffer the slightest grievance. 
It wasn't that Wan Yan couldn't bear to discipline A'Lang—a child's growth needs rules. But she never burdened him with expectations that shouldn't be placed on a child. Compared to other parents constantly nagging about hoping their son becomes a dragon, Wan Yan most often said, "Mother will listen to you." 
She knew from the start that her child didn't belong to her, but to himself. That he was willing to be born at her knee and call her 'Mother' was fortune spanning lifetimes. 

Wan Yan was Buddhist, often offering lamps before the Buddha even before marriage. 
After having A'Lang, she would light an extra lamp just for the child, in A'Lang's name. 
"My child, Mother lights this lamp for you, but you must know that any future glory is your own making." 
"When the time comes for you to fly away, don't feel bound by me." 
"But whenever you're tired, Mother will always keep a home for you."
I feel a little better now... thank you.
Silent, Unfinished Summer

zh: 昔有鹦鹉，飞集他山中，山中百鸟畜兽，转相重爱不相残害。鹦鹉自念：「虽尔，不可久也，当归耳。」便去。却后数月，大山失火四面皆然，鹦鹉遥见便入水，以羽翅取水飞上空中，以衣毛间水洒之，欲灭大火。如是往来。往来天神言：「咄鹦鹉！汝何以痴？千里之火宁为汝两翅水灭乎？」鹦鹉曰：「我由知而不灭也，我曾客是山中，山中百鸟畜兽皆仁善，悉为兄弟，我不忍见之耳。」天神感其至意，则雨灭火也。
en: Once there was a parrot that flew and alighted in another mountain. In the mountain, all the birds and beasts respected and loved each other, not harming one another. The parrot thought to itself: "Even so, I cannot stay long. I should return home." So it left. Several months later, a great mountain caught fire, blazing on all sides. Seeing it from afar, the parrot entered the water, took water in its wings, flew into the air, and sprinkled the water from its feathers, wanting to extinguish the great fire. It went back and forth like this. A celestial being said: "Hey, parrot! Why are you so foolish? How could a fire spanning a thousand miles be extinguished by the water from your two wings?" The parrot said: "I know it cannot be extinguished. But I was once a guest in this mountain. All the birds and beasts of the mountain were benevolent and kind, all were brothers. I cannot bear to see it." The celestial being, moved by its sincerity, then rained down and extinguished the fire.

zh: 凡猘狗啮人，七日辄一发，过三七日不发，则无苦也。要过百日，方大免耳。当终身禁食犬肉及蚕蛹，食此，发则死不可救矣。疮未愈之间，禁食生鱼、猪、鸡、腻。过一年禁之乃佳。但于饮下饭蒸鱼，及于肥器中食便发。若人曾食落葵得犬啮者，自难治。若疮瘥十数年后，食落葵便发。
en: When bitten by a rabid dog, symptoms typically appear in seven-day cycles. If no symptoms arise after three cycles, the danger lessens, but true safety comes only after one hundred days. The patient must abstain for life from dog meat and silkworm pupae; ingestion can trigger a fatal relapse. Before the wound fully heals, avoid eating raw fish, pork, chicken, and greasy foods. Ideally, avoid such foods for a full year. Even food steamed with fish below, or served in greasy utensils, may cause relapse. Those who've eaten Malabar spinach before being bitten are much harder to treat. Even ten years after healing, eating Malabar spinach may cause recurrence.

zh:
时值暮秋，苦风萧瑟。
他单衫草鞋，走在不熟悉的山路上，瑟缩慢步。
“家”已经不能回了。而远亲收留他的那间柴棚，甚至不能遮风避雨。
远处山下的灯火隔着雾，愈发飘渺。离得更远再看，像从水底仰望人间。

他想起那位戏台上的覆面将军，孤身一人，在千军万马中突围。
歌声无法驱散黑暗。更糟的是招来山间走兽，抑或不怀好意的流寇。
但他顾不上这许多。
心跳声如那日的重鼓，将军一往无前，声犹激越。

他奔跑着，朝向灯火的方向。
火光映映，渐渐能听见琵琶声声缭绕，喝彩声不绝。
这是他第二次来到戏台。
明明是草木凋萎的时节，他闭上双眼之前，却看见千树万树，梨雪飘坠。

“我等胡儿，吐气如电。
我采顶雷，踏石如泥。右得士力，
左得鞭回。日光西没，东西若月。
舞乐打去，录录长曲。”

顾秋华，湖州人氏，生具音律之才。
幼年为梨园弟子程肃所救，后拜入回雪舫。其天赋卓绝，音色清越，《兰陵王入阵曲》尤佳。
en:
It was late autumn, and the wind had turned sharp and bitter. 
Dressed in a thin shirt and straw sandals, he made his way down an unfamiliar mountain path, shivering as he walked. 
There was no "home" left to return to. And the shed his distant relatives had given him wasn't even enough to keep out the rain, let alone the wind. 
Down below, the lights of the valley flickered through the mist, growing fainter the farther he went—as if he were looking up at the world from the bottom of a lake. 

He thought of the masked general on the stage, alone in a sea of soldiers, carving a path through countless foes. 
A song could not keep the darkness at bay. Worse, it might draw the attention of mountain beasts or passing bandits. 
But none of that mattered to him now. 
His heartbeat pounded like the war drums from that day, the general surging forward, fearless and unshaken. 

He ran—toward the distant glow of firelight. 
As the glow deepened, he began to hear it: the spiraling notes of a pipa, the cheers and cries of the crowd. 
It was his second time standing before the stage. 
Though the season was one of withered grass and falling leaves, the moment before he closed his eyes, he saw pear blossoms—thousands of them—snowing down from unseen branches. 

"We breathe lightning. 
I grasp thunder above my head, grind stone soft beneath my feet. Strength in my right hand, 
command in my left. When the sun sets in the west, the east rises silver as the moon. 
Beat the drums—let the long song roll." 

Gu Qiuhua, a native of Huzhou, was born with music in his bones. 
As a child, he was saved by Cheng Su of the Masked Troupe and later joined the Pavilion of Returning Snow. His talent was unmatched, his voice clear and bright—
and of all his performances, none surpassed The Prince Enters the Formation.
